# Assertions for Mobile Tests

Add assertions to Endtest Mobile Tests for iOS and Android: assert on element presence, text, attributes, screen state, and natural-language conditions.

Part of the Endtest documentation (Mobile Tests). Canonical URL: https://endtest.io/docs/mobile-tests/assertions-for-mobile-tests

---
## Introduction
    
We need assertions to know if our test execution was successful or not. If we do not add assertions in our test cases, the values for `Passed` and `Failed` will be zero. A test case can have more than one assertion.
    
## Solution
    
Assertions can be added by using the `Add Assertion` action. You can choose from the following types of assertions:
    
| **Assertion Type**                   | **Description**                                                                       |
|--------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Element Is Present**               | Checks if an element is present                                                       |
| **Element Is Not Present**           | Checks if an element is not present                                                   |
| **Element Matches Value**            | Checks if the text from an element matches a certain value                           |
| **Element Does Not Match Value**     | Checks if the text from an element does not match a certain value                    |
| **Element Contains Value**           | Checks if the text from an element contains a certain value                          |
| **Element Does Not Contain Value**   | Checks if the text from an element does not contain a certain value                  |
| **Element Contains Attribute**       | Checks if an element contains a certain attribute                                    |
| **Element Does Not Contain Attribute** | Checks if an element does not contain a certain attribute                          |
| **Variable Assertion**               | Provides multiple ways to check a variable                                           |
| **Page Source Contains Value**       | Checks if the Page Source contains a certain value                                   |
| **Page Source Does Not Contain Value** | Checks if the Page Source does not contain a certain value                         |
| **Visual Assertion**                 | Performs a visual comparison between the screen or an element and a baseline screenshot. Details in the [Visual AI](https://endtest.io/docs/advanced/visual-ai) chapter. |
    

[Video](https://endtest-videos.s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/documentation/endtest_mobile_tests_assertions.mp4)

---

# IF Statements for Mobile Tests

Use IF statements in Endtest Mobile Tests to branch logic based on element visibility, text content, or variable values at runtime, on iOS and Android.

Part of the Endtest documentation (Mobile Tests). Canonical URL: https://endtest.io/docs/mobile-tests/if-statements-for-mobile-tests

---
## Introduction
    
An **If Statement** is a conditional statement that, if proven true, performs a number of steps.
    
There are certain scenarios where we need to execute some steps only if a certain condition is met.
    
**IF Statements** can be nested within other IF Statements.
    
An **IF Statement** can cross the boundary of a test case and continue into the next test case.
    
    
## If Statements
    
**IF Statements** can be added by using the `Start If Statement` action.
    
In order to close an **IF Statement**, you need to use the `End If Statement` action.
    
You can choose from the following types of **IF Statements**:
    
| **If Condition Type**               | **Description**                                                                       |
|-------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Element Is Present**              | Checks if an element is present                                                       |
| **Element Is Not Present**          | Checks if an element is not present                                                   |
| **Element Matches Value**           | Checks if the text from an element matches a certain value                           |
| **Element Does Not Match Value**    | Checks if the text from an element does not match a certain value                    |
| **Element Contains Value**          | Checks if the text from an element contains a certain value                          |
| **Element Does Not Contain Value**  | Checks if the text from an element does not contain a certain value                  |
| **Element Contains Attribute**      | Checks if an element contains a certain attribute                                    |
| **Element Does Not Contain Attribute** | Checks if an element does not contain a certain attribute                          |
| **Variable Assertion**              | Provides multiple ways to check a variable                                           |
| **Page Source Contains Value**      | Checks if the Page Source contains a certain value                                   |
| **Page Source Does Not Contain Value** | Checks if the Page Source does not contain a certain value                         |
| **Screen Matches Screenshot**       | Performs a visual comparison between the entire screen and a baseline screenshot      |
| **Element Matches Screenshot**      | Performs a visual comparison between an element and a baseline screenshot            |
    

[Video](https://endtest-videos.s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/documentation/endtest_mobile_tests_if_statement.mp4)

    
    
## Else Statements
    
You can also use **Else Statements** with the `Start Else Statement` and `End Else Statement` actions.
    
An **Else Statement** is an alternative statement that is executed if the result of a previous **If Statement** evaluates to false.
    
### Example Usage
    
```markdown
1. **Start If Statement**
   - Condition: Element Is Present
   - Locator: `//android.widget.TextView[@text='Login']`
   
2. **Steps to execute if condition is true:**
   - Click on the Login button
   - Enter username and password
   
3. **Start Else Statement**
   
4. **Steps to execute if condition is false:**
   - Navigate to the Registration page
   - Enter registration details
   
5. **End Else Statement**
6. **End If Statement**

---

# How to Scroll in Mobile Tests

Scroll in Endtest Mobile Tests for iOS and Android: scroll to an element, scroll inside lists, swipe screens, and reliably handle lazy-loaded content.

Part of the Endtest documentation (Mobile Tests). Canonical URL: https://endtest.io/docs/mobile-tests/how-to-scroll-in-mobile-tests

---
## Introduction
    
Our engine for Mobile Tests uses Appium to locate and interact with elements in native and hybrid mobile applications.
    
Appium does not provide direct `Scroll` or `Swipe` actions.
    
However, we can achieve the same effect with a `Flick` action or a `Move` action.
    
We simply need to flick or move in the opposite direction of the desired scroll or swipe.
    
## Options
    
### 1. Using the `Flick` action
    
The `Flick` action requires **3 parameters**:
    
- **Locator Type**
- **Locator**
- **Offset to flick by**
    
![Endtest Flick](https://app.endtest.io/images/endtest_mobile_flick.png)
    
The value for the `Offset to flick by` is comprised of an **X offset** and a **Y offset**, separated by a comma.
    
The offset is equivalent to the scrolling distance in this case.
    
As you can see, we need an element in order to flick.
    
The `Flick` action does not work with all elements, and there is no attribute to indicate if an element is suitable or not.
    
If an element is not suitable for the `Flick` action, performing that action on that element will not result in a scroll on that page.
    
You will not see any errors in the logs in that case; you will just notice that it has no effect.
    
This is because the element was located and the action was performed, but Appium does not throw any errors if the `Flick` action did not result in a scroll.
    
 Try performing the `Flick` action with different elements until you find one that works. It's a trial and error process. 
    
 
 For some applications, you might get an error that the `Flick` action is not supported. This is because the default versions of Appium used by BrowserStack might not support the `Flick` action for some applications. In this case, you can try changing the `Appium Version` from the `Settings` section of that test suite. 
    
    
### 2. Using the `Move` action
    
The `Move` action requires **3 parameters**:
    
- **Locator Type**
- **Locator**
- **Destination**

![Endtest Move](https://app.endtest.io/images/move_for_docs.png)
    
The value for the `Destination` is comprised of an **X coordinate** and a **Y coordinate**, separated by a comma.
    
As you can see, we need an element in order to move.
    
The `Move` action does not work with all elements, and there is no attribute to indicate if an element is suitable or not.
    
If an element is not suitable for the `Move` action, performing that action on that element will not result in a scroll on that page.
    
You will not see any errors in the logs in that case; you will just notice that it has no effect.
    
This is because the element was located and the action was performed, but Appium does not throw any errors if the `Move` action did not result in a scroll.
    
 Try performing the `Move` action with different elements until you find one that works. It's a trial and error process. 
    
    
## Scroll Types
    
### 1. Scroll Down
    
To scroll down, we must flick up or move up.
    
- **Using the `Flick` action:**  
  Add a **negative value** for the Y offset:  
  `0, -500`
    
- **Using the `Move` action:**  
  Add a **small non-negative value** for the Y coordinate:  
  `0, 0`
    
    
### 2. Scroll Up
    
To scroll up, we must flick down or move down.
    
- **Using the `Flick` action:**  
  Add a **positive value** for the Y offset:  
  `0, 500`
    
- **Using the `Move` action:**  
  Add a **large non-negative value** for the Y coordinate:  
  `0, 500`
    
    
### 3. Scroll Left
    
To scroll left, we must flick right or move right.
    
- **Using the `Flick` action:**  
  Add a **positive value** for the X offset:  
  `500, 0`
    
- **Using the `Move` action:**  
  Add a **large non-negative value** for the X coordinate:  
  `500, 0`
    
    
### 4. Scroll Right
    
To scroll right, we must flick left or move left.
    
- **Using the `Flick` action:**  
  Add a **negative value** for the X offset:  
  `-500, 0`
    
- **Using the `Move` action:**  
  Add a **small non-negative value** for the X coordinate:  
  `0, 0`

---

# Performing Complex Gestures

Perform pinch, zoom, multi-touch, drag, swipe, and long-press gestures in Endtest Mobile Tests, for both iOS and Android applications.

Part of the Endtest documentation (Mobile Tests). Canonical URL: https://endtest.io/docs/mobile-tests/performing-complex-gestures

---
## Introduction
    
In some scenarios, your test might need to perform complex gestures.
    
For example, pinching and zooming on a map.
    
You can combine multiple `Touch Actions` into a `Sequence`
    
Additionally, you can combine multiple `Sequences` into a `Multi Touch Actions Sequence`.
    
## Actions
    
### 1. Set Touch Action
    
The `Set Touch Action` allows you to define a **Touch Action**:
    
- **Tap and Hold**
- **Move**
- **Release**
    
![Endtest Set Touch Action](https://app.endtest.io/images/set_touch_action_docs.jpg)
    
**Names** must be provided for each `Touch Action`.
    
These names will be used when executing the `Touch Actions` or when combining them into a `Sequence`.
    
 Adding a `Set Touch Action` step will **not** execute that `Touch Action` it will only define it. 
    
### 2. Execute Touch Actions Sequence
    
After defining the `Touch Actions` with `Set Touch Action` steps, you can execute them with an `Execute Touch Actions Sequence` step.
    
The **names** of the defined `Touch Actions` must be provided, separated by `+` signs.
    
![Endtest Execute Touch Actions Sequence](https://app.endtest.io/images/execute_touch_actions_doc.jpg "Endtest Execute Touch Actions Sequence")
    
### 3. Set Touch Actions Sequence
    
This action can be used if you want to store multiple `Touch Actions` in a `Sequence`.
    
 Adding a `Set Touch Actions Sequence` step will **not** execute the `Sequence`; it will only define it. 
    
![Endtest Set Touch Actions Sequence](https://app.endtest.io/images/set_touch_actions_sequence.jpg "Endtest Set Touch Actions Sequence")
    
**Names** must be provided for each `Sequence`.
    
These names will be used when executing the `Sequences`.
    
    
### 4. Execute Multi Touch Actions Sequence
    
This action can be used to execute multiple `Sequences` at the same time.
    
A good example is when you want to pinch and zoom on a map.
    
Both fingers would perform separate `Sequences` simultaneously.
    
![Endtest Execute Multi Touch Actions Sequence](https://app.endtest.io/images/execute_multi_touch_actions_sequence.jpg)
    
The **names** of the defined `Sequences` must be provided, separated by `+` signs.

> To understand a complex gesture, it's best to first break down that gesture into `Sequences`.
> 
> Then, break down those `Sequences` into `Touch Actions`.
> 
> For example, pinching and zooming on a map is a gesture.
> 
> That gesture is made up of 2 `Sequences`.
> 
> Each finger will perform a separate `Sequence` simultaneously.
> 
> Each `Sequence` is defined by 3 `Touch Actions` (`Tap`, `Move`, `Release`), executed one after another.

---

# AI Test Creation Agent

Create Web Tests faster through an agentic approach that generates test steps from natural language instructions

Part of the Endtest documentation (Advanced). Canonical URL: https://endtest.io/docs/advanced/ai-test-creation-agent

---
## Overview

The **AI Test Creation Agent** helps you create Web Tests faster through an agentic approach that generates test steps based on your instructions.

You can access it by clicking the `New Test Suite` button and then selecting the `Use AI` option.

[Video](https://endtest-videos.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/documentation/endtest_AI_Test_Creation_Agent.webm)

Endtest is an agentic AI platform for test automation, designed to let AI actively participate in the test creation workflow while still producing clear, structured, and maintainable results inside the Endtest platform.

The AI Test Creation Agent is one of the many AI-powered components in Endtest, built to help teams accelerate test creation while keeping full visibility and control over the final result.

Unlike black-box approaches where an AI instruction remains inside the test at runtime, the Endtest AI Test Creation Agent generates regular test steps that can be reviewed, modified, and reused just like any other steps in Endtest.

This gives you visibility into what the test will do, control over the final result, and a more predictable test creation workflow.

## Why the Endtest approach is different

Many AI-based approaches in test automation focus on generating raw code or on leaving an AI-driven instruction inside the test itself.

In practice, those approaches can create maintenance overhead, instability, and unnecessary complexity. Users may end up reviewing hallucinated output, fixing brittle code, or repeatedly asking AI to repair earlier AI-generated changes.

Endtest does not rely on a generic, one-size-fits-all AI approach for test creation.

Using a general-purpose foundation model by itself is not enough to deliver the speed, consistency, and reliability required for production test automation. On their own, such models can be too slow for interactive workflows and can introduce hallucinations or unstable output.

That is why Endtest takes a different approach.

The AI Test Creation Agent is purpose-built for test automation and designed to generate clear, reusable, and editable test steps that fit naturally into the Endtest platform.

This is not something users typically get by calling a general-purpose model API directly, because the value comes from the full system rather than the model alone.

The advantage of AI in test automation is a higher-level layer that helps accelerate and democratize test automation.

## Built on a mature test automation platform

For more than 10 years, teams have used Endtest as a reliable platform for test automation.

That experience helped shape the AI Test Creation Agent around what users actually need: speed, clarity, control, and the ability to automate real-world workflows.

The AI capabilities are part of a mature platform that can automate complex flows, including emails, SMS messages, API requests, database calls, file uploads, file downloads, and more.

This means the AI Test Creation Agent is built into a platform that can support the full complexity of modern test automation.

## How to start using the AI Test Creation Agent

To start using the AI Test Creation Agent:

1. Go to the [Web Tests](https://app.endtest.io/tests) section.
2. Click the `New Test Suite` button.
3. Select the `Use AI` option.

If the agent is started directly from the Web Tests section, you need to provide the **Starting URL** at the beginning of the process.

That URL must be accessible to Endtest so the agent can open the application and interact with it.

In most cases, this means using a public URL. If your application is not publicly accessible, you can allow access by whitelisting the Endtest IP addresses or by using tunneling.

For more details, see the [Web Applications with restricted access](https://endtest.io/docs/web-tests/web-applications-with-restricted-access) chapter.

After starting the agent, you can choose between two approaches: `Granular` and `High-Level`.

## Granular and High-Level approaches

### Granular

In `Granular` mode, you provide instructions for individual steps.

You can add one step at a time or provide multiple steps at once.

This approach is useful when you want more precision and tighter control over what the agent generates.

### High-Level

In `High-Level` mode, you provide broader directions for the flow you want to automate.

The agent then generates the corresponding test steps for that flow.

This approach is useful when you want to move faster and describe the intended workflow at a higher level.

## Use files in the prompt

You can also use files in the prompt to provide additional context to the agent.

This can help when the test creation process depends on structured information, detailed instructions, or supporting documents that you want the agent to take into account.

## Configure the remote machine in the Endtest cloud

The AI Test Creation Agent includes settings for configuring the remote machine in the Endtest cloud where it runs.

You can configure settings such as:

1. Platform
2. Operating system
3. Browser
4. Browser version
5. Screen resolution

This helps you create tests in an environment that matches the setup you want to target, without relying on your own computer or infrastructure.

Because the AI Test Creation Agent generates standard Endtest steps, the resulting test remains fully compatible with all supported browsers.

This means the test can later be executed on any browser available in the Endtest cloud, including **Safari**.

## Start AI-driven test creation from an existing test

The AI Test Creation Agent can also be started from a specific point inside an existing test.

To do this, you can manually add a `Miscellaneous -> Start AI Test Creation Agent` step in your test.

When the test execution reaches that step, the AI Test Creation Agent starts from that point in the workflow.

In that case, you do not need to provide a Starting URL, because the agent continues from the current state reached by the test.

You can then create additional steps based on the current state of the application and save those steps either in the original test case or in a different test case.

This is especially useful when part of the workflow is already covered by an existing test and you want the agent to continue from that point, without having to generate the earlier steps again.

## Clear and reusable output

The generated output consists of regular test steps.

Those steps can be reviewed, modified, and reused just like any other steps in Endtest.

This makes the AI Test Creation Agent easier to trust and easier to maintain over time, because the final result is transparent and editable.

## When to use the AI Test Creation Agent

The AI Test Creation Agent is a strong choice when you want to reduce manual work and create tests faster.

It is especially useful when you want to:

1. Create tests quickly from natural language instructions
2. Accelerate the automation of common user flows
3. Continue automation from a specific point in an existing test
4. Use AI as a high-level layer to make test automation more accessible

## Conclusion

The Endtest AI Test Creation Agent combines agentic test creation with the control and maintainability of a mature test automation platform.

Instead of relying on a black-box runtime approach, it generates clear and editable test steps that fit naturally into the broader Endtest ecosystem.

This helps teams move faster while still keeping full visibility and control over their automated tests.

---

# Endtest Bot

An AI-powered autonomous QA colleague that works non-stop in the background to explore your web application and create automated Web Tests.

Part of the Endtest documentation (Advanced). Canonical URL: https://endtest.io/docs/advanced/endtest-bot

---
Endtest Bot is an **AI-powered, autonomous QA colleague** that can work **non-stop in the background** to explore a web application, discover useful scenarios, create automated Web Tests, and add completed tests to your Endtest account.

Endtest Bot is currently available as a **Beta** feature.

[Video](https://endtest-videos.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/documentation/endtest_bot.mp4)

Instead of requiring you to describe and create every test individually, Endtest Bot can take a broader QA assignment and autonomously continue exploring, creating, checking, and organizing tests over time.

Unlike the [AI Test Creation Agent](https://endtest.io/docs/advanced/ai-test-creation-agent), which is designed for creating a particular test from your instructions while you are actively working with the test editor, Endtest Bot is designed for longer-running, autonomous AI testing work in the background.

The tests created by Endtest Bot are regular Endtest Web Tests. You can open them, review the steps, edit them, execute them, add them to schedules, or use them in CI/CD just like tests created manually or with the AI Test Creation Agent.

## Starting Endtest Bot

To create a new Bot assignment:

1. Go to the **Web Tests** section.
2. Click the **Endtest Bot** button next to **New Test Suite**.
3. Select **Generate tests**.
4. Complete the setup wizard.

The Bot will verify that the Starting URL can be opened from the selected Endtest cloud environment before the assignment starts.

If the application is not publicly accessible, see [Web Applications with Restricted Access](https://endtest.io/docs/web-tests/web-applications-with-restricted-access).

## 1. Choose the web application

Enter the **Starting URL** for the web application that the Bot should explore.

For example:

```text
https://example.com
```

The Starting URL must begin with `http://` or `https://`.

You can also open **Run configuration** on this screen to choose the environment that the Bot should use.

The available settings include:

- Platform
- Operating System or Device
- Browser
- Browser Version
- Screen Resolution or Orientation
- Geolocation

The same run configuration is used while the Bot explores the application and when it checks the tests that it creates.

## 2. Choose how the Bot should get access

You can choose one of the following access modes.

### No credentials required

Use this option when the application or the functionality that you want to test is available without signing in.

### Use an existing account

Provide a username or email address and password.

The Bot can use that account to explore authenticated functionality and create tests for signed-in workflows.

For best results, use a dedicated test account instead of a production user account.

### Create a new account

Use this option when the application supports first-party signup and you want the Bot to create its own test account.

When possible, the Bot uses a fresh Endtest Mailbox address for the signup flow. This allows it to create tests for scenarios that include email verification.

Creating a new account requires permission to **Create data**, so that permission is enabled automatically when this access mode is selected.

Endtest Bot does not autonomously sign in through third-party identity providers such as Google, Microsoft, GitHub, Apple, Facebook, or LinkedIn.

## 3. Choose what the Bot should cover

You can give the Bot a broad assignment or tell it exactly which functionality to automate.

### Find useful functionality

The Bot explores the application and identifies useful workflows that can be automated.

This can include navigation, authentication, forms, validation behavior, common user journeys, and other functionality discovered while the Bot builds its QA Map.

### Only specific functionality

Use this option when you already know which flows you want automated.

Enter separate flows on separate lines, for example:

```text
Invite a team member
Create a project
Search and filter orders
```

You can provide up to 12 specific flows in one assignment.

## 4. Choose the testing types

All testing types are selected by default. You can disable the ones that are not relevant to the assignment.

The available testing types are:

- **Positive testing**: happy paths and expected user workflows.
- **Negative testing**: invalid inputs, rejected actions, and failure cases.
- **Functional variations**: different realistic ways users can perform the main workflow.
- **Boundary & edge cases**: minimums, maximums, empty values, and unusual conditions.
- **Validation testing**: required fields, formats, constraints, and business-rule validation.
- **Error & recovery testing**: failure handling, retries, and recovery states.
- **Accessibility testing**: accessibility checks and reports on representative pages.

The initial website exploration still runs even when some testing types are disabled, because it gives the Bot the basic information it needs to understand the application.

## 5. Set data-change permissions

Endtest Bot can interact with application data, but you control what it is allowed to change.

The available permissions are:

- **Create data**: create new accounts, records, or items.
- **Edit data**: change existing records.
- **Delete data**: remove existing records.

These permissions are hard limits for autonomous Bot work.

For example, if **Delete data** is disabled, the Bot should not create a test that deletes an existing record simply because it discovers a Delete button during exploration.

Even when the corresponding permissions are enabled, the Bot avoids high-impact actions such as purchases, billing changes, security changes, and sending real external messages.

For applications with important production data, we recommend giving the Bot a dedicated test environment or dedicated test account whenever possible.

## 6. Add supporting information

You can provide optional **Supporting notes** with information that may help the Bot understand the application.

For example:

```text
Staging data resets every night.
The Orders page is under Operations.
Use the Demo workspace for all tests.
```

You can also attach supporting files such as screenshots, PDFs, documents, spreadsheets, CSV files, text files, Markdown files, HTML files, JSON, XML, YAML, or log files.

You can attach up to 4 files, with a maximum of 4 MB per file and 12 MB in total.

Endtest also sends email updates when tests are ready or when the Bot needs input from you.

## 7. Access check

Before the assignment starts, Endtest launches the selected cloud environment and verifies that the Starting URL is accessible.

If the URL can be opened, the Bot assignment starts automatically.

If the URL cannot be reached, Endtest shows the access problem instead of starting an assignment that cannot make progress.

Applications behind a firewall, VPN, IP allowlist, or other network restriction may require additional configuration. See [Web Applications with Restricted Access](https://endtest.io/docs/web-tests/web-applications-with-restricted-access).

## What the Bot does in the background

Once the assignment starts, you can close the Endtest Bot window or leave the Web Tests page.

Endtest Bot is designed to work **autonomously and non-stop in the background**, without requiring you to keep the Endtest interface open. Its AI explores the application, creates candidate tests, checks them, and gradually builds coverage for the assignment.

Depending on the application and the selected settings, it can create tests for scenarios such as:

- website and page navigation;
- positive user workflows;
- invalid login or signup behavior;
- first-party signup and email verification;
- login and logout;
- form validation;
- boundary and negative scenarios;
- requested application workflows;
- accessibility checks;
- additional scenarios discovered from the QA Map.

The Bot avoids creating exact duplicate scenarios when equivalent coverage already exists in the same assignment.

Related tests can be grouped into suites such as Authentication, Accessibility, Navigation, Primary Workflows, or Requested Workflows.

For authentication flows, the Bot can also create reusable components so that later tests can reuse common setup such as variables or Login instead of recording the same authentication sequence repeatedly.

## How generated tests are checked

Endtest Bot does not publish every generated draft immediately.

For most scenarios, the Bot first creates the test and then runs an internal check to confirm that the generated test can execute successfully before it is added to your visible Web Tests.

If a generated test is not reliable yet, the Bot can retry it later instead of immediately adding an unreliable test to your account.

These internal Bot validation executions are not shown in the normal **Results** page.

The generated tests themselves are normal Endtest tests and can be executed normally afterward. See [How to Execute Web Tests](https://endtest.io/docs/web-tests/how-to-execute-web-tests).

## Accessibility tests

When **Accessibility testing** is enabled, Endtest Bot can add Accessibility Check steps to representative pages that it discovers.

Bot-generated Accessibility Check steps use **Fail step on severity: Serious** by default. This means Serious and Critical accessibility violations can cause the Accessibility Check step to fail, while Moderate and Minor findings remain informational.

An accessibility assertion that finds a Serious or Critical issue is not treated by Endtest Bot as evidence that the generated test itself is broken. The test can still be published because the failed accessibility assertion represents a real finding that the test was designed to detect.

For more information about accessibility checks, see [Accessibility Testing](https://endtest.io/docs/web-tests/accessibility-testing).

## Bot Activity

Open **Endtest Bot → Bot activity** to follow current and previous assignments.

Bot Activity shows information such as:

- the website being tested;
- the current URL;
- the task that the Bot is currently working on;
- recently completed activity;
- generated tests;
- tests that need another attempt;
- requests for user input;
- links for opening completed tests.

The activity feed also exposes observable browser artifacts when available, including:

- **Screenshot**
- **Page source (.txt)**

These artifacts can be useful when you want to understand what the Bot saw while it was exploring a page or creating a test.

Older activity entries can be expanded with **Show earlier entries**.

The activity feed shows observable actions and progress. It does not expose private model reasoning or chain-of-thought.

## QA Map

Each Bot assignment can build a **QA Map** of the application as it explores.

The QA Map can include:

- public pages;
- authentication areas;
- Login and Sign Up branches;
- authenticated application areas;
- discovered functionality;
- planned scenarios;
- URLs associated with branches;
- tests that have been linked to those branches.

You can expand or collapse individual branches, or use **Expand all** and **Collapse all**.

A test linked to a QA Map branch represents **partial coverage**, not complete coverage.

For example, a Login branch may eventually contain separate tests for successful login, invalid credentials, required fields, password validation, account-lock behavior, and other scenarios. Creating one Login test does not mean that the entire Login branch is considered fully tested.

The QA Map helps Endtest Bot continue exploring useful gaps without repeatedly creating the same scenario.

## Pausing, resuming, and stopping the Bot

An active assignment can be controlled from Bot Activity.

### Pause after current task

The Bot finishes the task that it is currently working on and then pauses the assignment.

You can resume it later.

### Resume

Continue a paused assignment from its existing progress.

The Bot does not need to restart the assignment from the beginning.

### Stop after current task

The Bot finishes the current task and then stops the assignment.

Tests that were already completed remain in your account.

Deleting a Bot Activity history entry does not delete completed tests that were generated by that assignment.

## When the Bot needs input

Endtest Bot is designed to continue **autonomously** whenever its AI can make safe progress, so one blocked scenario does not necessarily stop the rest of the assignment.

If it reaches a scenario where real user input is required, it can mark that work as needing input while continuing with other independent tasks.

A request for input may include the URL, screenshot, and page source that were available when the Bot reached the blocking point.

Endtest also sends an email when the Bot needs input.

## CAPTCHA and human verification

Endtest Bot does not solve or bypass reCAPTCHA, hCaptcha, Cloudflare Turnstile, or similar human-verification systems.

If the Bot reaches human verification after completing useful first-party steps, it may preserve those completed steps as partial automation instead of discarding the entire flow.

For testing environments, you can often configure the application or verification provider so trusted Endtest traffic does not receive the challenge.

See [Dealing with reCAPTCHA](https://endtest.io/docs/web-tests/dealing-with-recaptcha).

## Tips for better Bot assignments

For better results:

1. Use a staging or test environment when the Bot is allowed to create or modify data.
2. Provide a dedicated test account for authenticated applications.
3. Use **Only specific functionality** when you have a small set of high-priority workflows that you want first.
4. Use supporting notes to explain application-specific terminology, unusual navigation, or test-data requirements.
5. Enable only the data-change permissions that the Bot actually needs.
6. Review Bot Activity and the QA Map to understand what has already been explored and where more coverage is being added.
7. Review generated tests before making them part of a release-blocking CI/CD pipeline, just as you would review tests created by a human or by another AI-assisted workflow.

## Endtest Bot vs. AI Test Creation Agent

Both features create regular, editable Endtest Web Tests, but they are designed for different workflows.

Use the **AI Test Creation Agent** when you want to actively create a particular test from your instructions.

Use **Endtest Bot** when you want an **autonomous AI QA workflow** that can work **non-stop in the background**, exploring the application and creating, checking, and organizing tests over time.

You can use both approaches in the same Endtest project.

---

# AI Assertions

Validate complex test conditions in Endtest using natural language. Describe what should be true on the page and let AI Assertions handle the rest.

Part of the Endtest documentation (Advanced). Canonical URL: https://endtest.io/docs/advanced/ai-assertions

---
## Overview

**AI Assertion** is an option available within the `Add Assertion` action.

It allows you to validate test conditions using natural language instead of classic assertions based on locators or fixed values.

Instead of asserting a single element, the AI evaluates the context provided by the selected **Assertion Scope** and determines whether the condition is met.

[Video](https://endtest.io/videos/ai_assertion_example.mp4)

## Assertion Scope Options

The `Assertion Scope` defines **what information the AI can analyze**. Only **one scope** can be selected per AI Assertion.

### Web Tests

#### 1. Web Page

When `Web Page` is selected, the AI processes:

- The current **URL**
- The full **page source (HTML)**
- A **screenshot** of the page

**Example prompts:**

- `Confirm that the page is in French`
- `Verify that the visible page content is free of grammar mistakes`
- `Check that the background includes a sports car`

#### 2. Cookies

Allows the AI to read and reason about browser cookies.

**Example prompts:**

- `Check that the cookies indicate an authenticated user session`
- `Verify the presence of a third-party analytics tracking cookie`

#### 3. Variables

Allows the AI to inspect previously defined test variables.

**Example prompts:**

- `Check that the $products variable is an array with at least 50 items`
- `Verify that the total cost correctly includes VAT based on the listed product prices`

#### 4. Test Execution Logs

Allows the AI to analyze the execution logs generated so far.

**Example prompts:**

- `Verify that there are no warnings so far`
- `Check that the test execution accessed at least 5 Wikipedia pages related to cars`
- `Verify that there was no Wait Until step that waited for more than 30 seconds`

### Mobile Tests

For Mobile Tests, web-specific scopes are replaced with `App Screen`.

#### 1. App Screen

When `App Screen` is selected, the AI processes:

- The **app screen source**
- A **screenshot** of the current screen

**Example prompts:**

- `Verify that the screen shows only pictures of dogs`
- `Confirm that this section is showing only books related to chemistry`
- `Verify that the map has loaded`

## Assertion Strictness Levels

Each AI Assertion allows you to control how strictly the condition is evaluated.

- **Strict**: The condition must be clearly and unambiguously true. Best for critical validations.
- **Standard**: Balanced interpretation with minor flexibility. Recommended for most tests.
- **Lenient**: Allows partial matches and ambiguity. Useful for unstable environments or early testing stages.

# AI Variables

Generate, extract, and transform data using natural language, with no custom scripts or locators required

Part of the Endtest documentation (Advanced). Canonical URL: https://endtest.io/docs/advanced/ai-variables

---
## Overview

**AI Variables** can be generated using the **Use AI** option within the **Set Variable** action.

They allow you to generate, extract, and transform data using natural language, without writing custom scripts or complex parsing logic.

AI Variables are especially useful when the data:

- Is dynamic or context-dependent
- Requires reasoning or aggregation
- Is difficult to extract reliably using a single locator

![endtest ai variables web page](https://endtest.io/images/ai_variables.jpg)

## Scope Options

The **Scope** defines **where the AI gets its information from**. Only **one scope** can be selected per AI Variable.

## Web Tests

### 1. General Knowledge

Uses general, real-world knowledge and does **not** depend on the application under test.

**Example prompts:**

- `Generate a random fictional mobile phone number from Sweden`
- `Generate a valid IBAN for Germany`

### 2. Web Page

When **Web Page** is selected, the AI processes:

- The current **URL**
- The **page source**
- A **screenshot** of the page

**Example prompts:**

- `Calculate the total value by adding up all the prices from the "Price" column from the table`
- `Identify the primary currency used on the page`
- `Extract the value represented by the largest segment of the pie chart`

### 3. Cookies

Extracts values from browser cookies.

**Example prompts:**

- `Extract the value of the cookie that contains the user session information`
- `Get the value of the Google Analytics _ga cookie`

### 4. Variables

Allows the AI to read, combine, and transform existing variables.

**Example prompts:**

- `Add up all the numerical values from the variables that contain the prices of the products`
- `Extract the customer ID from the nested JSON stored in the $responseBody variable`
- `Calculate the number of days between the start date and end date variables`

### 5. Test Execution Logs

Allows the AI to analyze execution logs and derive values.

**Example prompts:**

- `Get the number of total Click steps executed so far`
- `Extract the latest URL that was accessed in this test execution`

## Mobile Tests

For **Mobile Tests**, web-specific scopes are replaced with **App Screen**.

### 1. App Screen

When **App Screen** is selected, the AI processes:

- The **app screen source**
- A **screenshot** of the current screen

**Example prompts:**

- `Extract the option that is visually marked as recommended`
- `Get the name of the largest city shown on the map`
- `Extract the name of the main shopping category shown on the screen`

## Strictness Levels

When generating or extracting AI Variables, you can control how strict the AI should be.

1. **Strict**: Precise extraction. Fails if the value is unclear or ambiguous.
2. **Standard**: Balanced interpretation. Recommended for most use cases.
3. **Lenient**: Tolerant of ambiguity, formatting differences, or partial matches.

## Best Practices

- Be explicit about what value you want to generate or extract.
- Use **General Knowledge** only when the value does not depend on the application.
- Prefer **Standard** strictness for most variables.
- Use **Strict** strictness for values that affect critical test logic.

---

# AI Test Import

Import tests that were exported from other test automation tools.

Part of the Endtest documentation (Advanced). Canonical URL: https://endtest.io/docs/advanced/ai-test-import

---
## Introduction

Migrating from another test automation tool? Endtest can automatically import your existing tests, regardless of the format they were exported in.

The AI Test Import feature uses AI to analyze the structure of exported test files and convert each step into native Endtest steps. It supports JSON, CSV, TXT, and other formats from virtually any test automation tool.

[Video](https://endtest-videos.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/documentation/endtest_import_test_from_file_with_AI.mp4)

## How it works

1. Export your tests from your current tool (Selenium, Katalon, TestProject, etc.) in any supported format.
2. In Endtest, go to the import section and upload your file.
3. The AI analyzes the file format, identifies the structure, and maps each step to an Endtest test step.
4. Review the generated test and make any adjustments.

## Supported formats

Since the AI dynamically detects the format, it works with exports from most test automation tools:

- **JSON**: Structured test exports
- **CSV**: Spreadsheet-based test cases
- **TXT**: Plain text test scripts

Each tool has its own export format, but the AI handles the parsing automatically.

## Tips

- **Review after import**: While the AI does an excellent job of mapping steps, always review the imported test to ensure everything translated correctly.
- **Complex assertions**: Some tool-specific assertion types may need manual adjustment after import.
- **Variables and data**: If your original test used variables or data sources, you may need to reconfigure those in Endtest after import.

> **Note:** This feature makes it easy to migrate from tools like Selenium, Katalon, TestProject, Mabl, and others without having to manually recreate every test.

# Analyze Failures with AI

Use AI to investigate failed test steps, understand the likely cause, and get a suggested fix based on the execution evidence.

Part of the Endtest documentation (Advanced). Canonical URL: https://endtest.io/docs/advanced/analyze-failures-with-ai

---
The **Analyze failure with AI** feature can help you investigate failed test steps directly from the Results page.

Instead of reviewing the error message, screenshot, page source, and step configuration separately, you can ask Endtest to analyze the available execution evidence and explain what may have caused the failure.

![Analyze failure with AI popup](https://endtest.io/images/ai-failure-analysis.png)

> **Beta:** AI-powered test failure analysis is currently available as a Beta feature.

## How to analyze a failed step

1. Open the **Results** page for a test execution.
2. Select the **Logs** section.
3. Locate a failed assertion or a step that returned an error.
4. Click **Analyze failure with AI** below the failed step.
5. Wait for the analysis to be generated.

The popup displays the test case and step being analyzed, along with the diagnosis and any suggested changes.

## What the AI uses

Depending on the type of execution and the available evidence, Endtest can use:

- The complete error or assertion failure message.
- The test step configuration, including the action, locator, and parameters.
- The screenshot captured when the step failed.
- The page source captured at the time of the failure.
- The surrounding test and execution context.
- General knowledge about browser automation, Selenium, Appium, browser behavior, mobile applications, and common test failure patterns.

For web tests, the page source generally contains the DOM that was available when the failure occurred.

For mobile tests, the analysis can use the Appium page source and the available element information from the application interface.

The screenshot helps the AI compare what was visually displayed with what the test expected to find or verify.

## Understanding the analysis

The generated response can include the following sections:

### Diagnosis

A concise description of what appears to have failed.

For example, the analysis may determine that a stored locator no longer matches an element on the page.

### Likely cause

An explanation of the most probable reason for the failure.

Possible causes can include:

- An incorrect or outdated locator.
- An element that was not present or visible.
- A page that had not finished loading.
- A test running in the wrong browser tab, window, or iframe.
- A different authentication or application state.
- Changed test data or environment configuration.
- A browser, driver, device, or infrastructure issue.
- An assertion that no longer matches the current application behavior.

### Evidence

The specific information that supports the diagnosis.

This may include locator match counts, elements found in the page source, information visible in the screenshot, or details from the original error message.

### Suggested fix

A practical recommendation for correcting the test or investigating the application.

When the AI identifies a likely replacement value, such as a new XPath or another step parameter, it can display that value separately under **Use this in the step**.

You can use the copy button to copy the suggested value to your clipboard.

## Editing the step

Click **Edit step** to open the relevant test case in the test editor.

When the test case has been updated since the execution was completed, the original step may no longer have the same internal ID. In that situation, Endtest displays a warning explaining that the test case was updated and that its steps received new IDs.

The **Edit step** button will still open the relevant test case, but it may not automatically focus the exact historical step.

## When additional information is needed

Some failures cannot be diagnosed confidently from the captured evidence alone.

For example, multiple elements may look similar, or the intended target may not be clear from the locator and screenshot. In those situations, the analysis may ask you to describe the intended element or provide additional context.

Adding details such as the visible text, role, location, or expected behavior of the element can help produce a more useful analysis.

## Important considerations

AI-generated failure analysis is intended to assist with troubleshooting, but it may not always identify the exact cause.

A screenshot and page source represent the application at a specific moment in the execution. They may not include server logs, network responses, database state, application logs, or events that occurred before the evidence was captured.

Before updating a test, review the diagnosis and confirm that the suggested change matches the intended application behavior.

A failed test does not always mean that the test is incorrect. The failure may reveal a real application defect, an environment issue, or an unexpected change in the tested workflow.

---

# Variables

Use variables in Endtest tests to capture values, share state across steps, drive data-driven scenarios, and generate dynamic inputs with AI Variables.

Part of the Endtest documentation (Advanced). Canonical URL: https://endtest.io/docs/advanced/how-to-use-variables

---
## Introduction

It's considered a best practice to use variables in your tests.

This helps you avoid situations where you need to update the same value in multiple places.

## Declaring variables

You can use the `Set Variable` action to declare a new variable.

The options from the `Set Variable` action allow you to enter, extract or even generate values.

All variable names must start with the `$` character.

Once declared, a variable can be used across the entire test suite.

If you want to use it in other test suites, you have to import the test case in which the variable was declared.

### Variable Types for Web Tests

| Variable Type                             | Description                                                              |
|-------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Set Value                                 | Set a hardcoded value.                                                   |
| Set Password                              | Set a hardcoded masked value.                                            |
| Set Secret                                | Set a hardcoded masked value, protected by an extra layer of encryption. |
| Random Number                             | Generate a random number.                                                |
| Random String                             | Generate a random string.                                                |
| Random Email                              | Generate a random email address.                                         |
| Real Phone Number                         | Select one of the real phone numbers for testing assigned to your Team.  |
| Timestamp                                 | Generate a timestamp.                                                    |
| Use AI                                    | Details are provided in the [AI Variables](https://endtest.io/docs/advanced/ai-variables) chapter. |
| UUID (Universally Unique Identifier)      |  Generate a 128-bit universally unique identifier (UUID) |
| Generate OTP from Secret Key              |  Generate the OTP from a Secret Key, just like an Authenticator app.     |
| Extract Value from Element                | Extract the text from an element.                                        |
| Extract Value from Element with OCR       | Extract the text from an element by using Optical Character Recognition. |
| Extract Attribute from Element            | Extract the value of an attribute from an element.                       |
| Extract CSS Property from Element         | Extract the value of a CSS Property from an element.                     |
| Extract Value from JavaScript Variable    | Extract the value from a JavaScript variable.                            |
| Extract Value from Alert                  | Extract the text from an Alert box.                                      |
| Extract CSS Selector from Focused Element | Extract the CSS Selector from a focused element.                         |
| Extract Result from SQL Query             | Extract the results from a SQL query.                                    |
| Extract Latest SMS                        | Extract the latest SMS sent to a real phone number.                      |
| Extract Current URL                       | Extract the URL from the current page.                                   |
| Extract Current Title                     | Extract the title from the current page.                                 |
| Extract Number of Child Elements          | Extract the number of direct child elements from a parent element.       |
| Extract Number of Elements                | Extract the number of elements by providing a locator.                   |
| Extract Name of Most Recent Downloaded File | Extracts the name of the last downloaded file.                          |
| Extract Size of Most Recent Downloaded File | Extracts the size (bytes) of the last downloaded file.                   |
| Extract MIME Type of Most Recent Downloaded File | Extracts the MIME Type (case-sensitive) of the last downloaded file. |
| Link to Most Recent Downloaded File        | Returns a download link to the last downloaded file.                     |

 The Variable Types which involve randomness have mandatory inputs for rules which control that randomness. For example, the `Random Number` option requires users to declare a value for the `Length of Number`. And the `Random Email` option requires users to declare a value for the `Email Domain`. 

 The `Real Phone Number` and `Extract Latest SMS` options require your account to be associated with real phone numbers. We provide real phone numbers for our users. You don't have to use any external service. If there are no real phone numbers associated with your account, please contact our Support Team. More information is available in the [Read SMS](https://endtest.io/docs/advanced/read-sms) chapter. 

You can also declare variables directly in the Endtest API request for starting a test execution, more details are available in the [Endtest API](https://endtest.io/docs/advanced/how-to-use-the-endtest-api) chapter.

## Using variables

After you set a variable, you can use it in other steps or cases by simply entering its name in any input.

Simply typing `$` inside an input will display a dropdown with the available variables.

You can concatenate variables with strings or with other variables by placing the variable name between double curly brackets:  
`My name is {{$username}} and my email is {{$email}}`

You can also print the variables in the Results by using the `Variable` or `All Variables` options from the `Print in Results` action.
