# Waits

Use Waits in Endtest tests to handle dynamic content reliably. Wait Until, Pause, and Wait For Element steps replace flaky sleep-based waiting.

Part of the Endtest documentation (Advanced). Canonical URL: https://endtest.io/docs/advanced/waits

---
## Introduction

In a test, Wait commands direct test execution to pause for a certain length of time before moving onto the next step.

Endtest provides Smart Waits, and that means that you don't have to add a Wait before each interaction with an element.

But you also have the option of adding `Wait Until` and `Pause` steps, since certain situations might require these actions.

## 1. Smart Waits

There are 2 categories of Smart Waits:

1. Smart Waits for pages.
2. Smart Waits for elements.

### 1. Smart Waits for pages

When a page is accessed in a test, Endtest will automatically wait for that page to load, before attempting to execute other steps.

You can configure the `Page Load Timeout` in the `Advanced` section of the `Settings` for each test suite.

The `Page Load Timeout` is the maximum amount of time that the engine will wait for the page to load, before showing an error message.

### 2. Smart Waits for elements

Endtest will automatically wait for an element to be present, before attempting to interact with it.

The engine will look for that element 10 times every second, until it finds the element.

If it finds the element, it performs the action and then it immediately moves to the next step.

You can configure the `Element Load Timeout` in the `Advanced` section of the `Settings` for each test suite.

The `Element Load Timeout` is the maximum amount of time that the engine will wait for an element to be present, before showing an `Element not found` error message.

![endtest timeout wait](https://app.endtest.io/images/timeout_settings.jpg)

If you are running a test on an environment which is a bit slow, we recommend increasing the values for the `Element Load Timeout` and `Page Load Timeout` settings.

## 2. Wait Until

The `Wait Until` method can be found in the `Miscellaneous` action.

It's useful in situations where your test needs to wait for a certain condition.

![endtest wait until settings](https://app.endtest.io/images/wait_until_doc.jpg)

A relevant example is when your test needs to wait for an email to be delivered to the [Endtest Mailbox](https://endtest.io/docs/web-tests/how-to-test-emails).

There is no exact way to know how long it would take the system from your side to send the email.

A good approach is to wait to for the Email Subject element to be present.

And you can also refresh the page at a certain interval while waiting, which is useful for pages that do not auto-refresh their contents.

Adding a value in the `Maximum time to wait (s)` is mandatory, since you don't want that step to wait for a long time in case the email never gets sent from your side.

![endtest wait for email mailbox](https://app.endtest.io/images/wait_for_email_doc.jpg)

Another relevant example is when you need to wait for an element to be clickable.

Our engine will automatically wait for an element to be present, but not necessarily clickable.

There are scenarios where an element might appear on the page, and not be clickable yet.

Details about that are provided in the [Element not clickable](https://endtest.io/docs/web-tests/finding-elements-in-web-applications#2-element-not-clickable) section.

## 3. Pause

There is also the option to add a `Pause` step.

During that pause, the entire test execution will wait.

![endtest pause wait](https://app.endtest.io/images/pause_doc.jpg)

It's not considered a good practice to use `Pause` steps.

The recommended approach is to configure the `Element Load Timeout` and `Page Load Timeout` settings accordingly or to use `Wait Until` steps.

---

# Endtest API

Use the Endtest API to trigger test runs, fetch results, manage suites, and integrate Endtest into custom dashboards or release pipelines.

Part of the Endtest documentation (Advanced). Canonical URL: https://endtest.io/docs/advanced/how-to-use-the-endtest-api

---
## Introduction

You can easily integrate Endtest into your workflow by using our API.

These are the tasks you can perform with the Endtest API:
1. Start a test execution.
2. Start multiple test executions.
3. Fetch the results for a test execution.
4. Fetch the results for multiple test executions.
5. Stop a test execution.
6. Get the IDs and Names of all the test suites that you have access to.
7. Get the IDs, Names and External IDs of all the test cases from a test suite.
8. Upload a file in the [Drive Section](https://app.endtest.io/drive).
9. Get the list of files uploaded in the [Drive](https://app.endtest.io/drive).
10. Delete a file from the [Drive](https://app.endtest.io/drive).
11. Get the number of available parallel slots.
12. Get the list of Secure Gateway IP addresses.
13. Import test suite from JSON file.
14. Import Postman collection.
15. Manage External IDs for Test Cases.

## 1. Start a test execution

To get the API request for executing a test, just click on `Get API Request` from the Run Test Suite modal.

The API request contains the `appId` and `appCode` which are used to identify your user and do not change.

[Video](https://endtest-videos.s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/documentation/endtest_api.mp4)

 

This API request can only be called with an HTTP Method of type GET.

### Endtest API Parameters for starting a Web Test execution

| Endtest API Parameter   | Description                 |
|-------------------------|-----------------------------|
| action                  | The type of action (runWeb) |
| appId                   | The App ID of the user      |
| appCode                 | The App Code of the user    |
| suite                   | The ID of the test suite    |
| platform                | The platform to run the test on |
| os                      | The operating system for the execution |
| browser                 | The browser for the execution |
| browserVersion          | The browser version for the execution (latest or beta) |
| resolution              | The screen resolution for the execution |
| geolocation             | The Geolocation for the execution |
| cases                   | The test cases to be executed |
| notes                   | Notes that will appear in the execution |

### Endtest API Parameters for starting a Mobile Test execution

| Parameter | Description                               |
|-----------|-------------------------------------------|
| action    | The type of action (runMobile)            |
| appId     | The App ID of the user                    |
| appCode   | The App Code of the user                  |
| suite     | The ID of the test suite                  |
| platform  | The platform to run the test on           |
| device    | The mobile device to run the test on      |
| app       | The download link for the APK or IPA file |
| grid      | The mobile device grid provider           |
| cases     | The test cases to be executed             |
| notes     | Notes that will appear in the execution   |

The response from this API request contains a `hash` which can be used to uniquely identify that test execution.

### Declaring variables in the Endtest API request

You can add variables directly in the Endtest API request.

For example, adding `&username=Matt` will automatically create the variable `$username` with the value `Matt`.

### Overwriting the settings for Webhook Notifications

The Webhook URL and Webhook Notifications can be overwritten by adding `&webhookUrl=your_webhook_url` and `&webhookNotifications=option`, where option can be 0, 1 or 2.

0 = Do not send 
1 = Send every time a test runs 
2 = Send only when a test fails 

If your Webhook URL is `https://my-own-webhook.com` and you want to receive notifications every time a test is executed, you would need to add the following to your Endtest API call: 
`&webhookUrl=https://my-own-webhook.com&webhookNotifications=1`

### Partial match for the app parameter for Mobile Tests

The 'app' parameter for starting Mobile Tests can be a partial match.

For example, if we have this download link for an APK file:

`https://endtest-files.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/uzikStbflpt3PcQiM8z8ByYh1H/Master-Sample.apk`

The app parameter can look like this:

`&app="[*Master*.apk]"`

>- Double quotes should be added at the beginning and end of that value.
>- Square brackets should be added at the beginning and end, inside the double quotes.
>- The asterisk is a wildcard, can be placed wherever you want to replace 0 or more characters.
>- It will fetch the most recent uploaded file from the Endtest Drive that matches that pattern.
>- The pattern is not case-sensitive.
>- The `Visibility` property of the file from the Endtest Drive must be set to `MyEntireTeam`.

> **Note:** **Legacy Endtest API requests**     The Endtest API request for starting test executions was updated on October 12 2021. The legacy Endtest API requests are still supported.     You can download the legacy Endtest API Mappings for starting a web test execution here: [Endtest_API_Mappings_for_Web_Tests.pdf](https://endtest-files.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/6Z0PMGM06Y4iXYctL2KxExoB2KgGjP/Endtest_API_Mappings_for_Web_Tests.pdf)

## 2. Start multiple test executions

The only way to start multiple test executions with one single Endtest API request is by using [Labels](https://endtest.io/docs/advanced/team/#labels).

In the Endtest API request, replace the `suite` parameter with the `label` parameter and provide the name of the label instead of the test suite ID.

This API request can only be called with an HTTP Method of type GET.

### Endtest API Parameters for starting multiple Web Test executions

| Endtest API Parameter | Description                                 |
|-----------------------|---------------------------------------------|
| action                | The type of action (runWeb)                 |
| appId                 | The App ID of the user                      |
| appCode               | The App Code of the user                    |
| label                 | The label assigned to the test suites       |
| platform              | The platform to run the test on             |
| os                    | The operating system for the execution      |
| browser               | The browser for the execution               |
| browserVersion        | The browser version for the execution (latest or beta) |
| resolution            | The screen resolution for the execution     |
| geolocation           | The Geolocation for the execution           |
| cases                 | The test cases to be executed               |
| notes                 | Notes that will appear in the execution     |

### Endtest API Parameters for starting multiple Mobile Test executions

| Parameter | Description                               |
|-----------|-------------------------------------------|
| action    | The type of action (runMobile)            |
| appId     | The App ID of the user                    |
| appCode   | The App Code of the user                  |
| label     | The label assigned to the test suites     |
| platform  | The platform to run the test on           |
| device    | The mobile device to run the test on      |
| app       | The download link for the APK or IPA file |
| grid      | The mobile device grid provider           |
| cases     | The test cases to be executed             |
| notes     | Notes that will appear in the execution   |

The request will respond with the unique hashes for each test execution, separated by commas.

>The value from the `label` parameter is case-sensitive.
>
>Only one Label Name can be provided in the `label` parameter for each request.
>
>Only one configuration can be provided in each request.

## 3. Fetch the results for a test execution

To get the results from a test execution with our API, use a GET request with the following format:

`https://app.endtest.io/api.php?action=getResults&appId=[your app id]&appCode=[your app code]&hash=[the returned hash]&format=[html or json or json-light]`

Replace `[your app id]` and `[your app code]` with your `appId` and `appCode` values, which you can retrieve from the [Settings](https://app.endtest.io/settings) page by clicking on the `Show API Credentials` button.

Replace `[the returned hash]` with the hash that was returned by the Endtest API request for starting a test execution.

You have the option to choose a format, either `html` or `json` or `json-light`.

This API request can only be called with an HTTP Method of type GET.

| Endtest API Parameter | Description                                     |
|-----------------------|-------------------------------------------------|
| action                | The type of action (getResults)                |
| appId                 | The App ID of the user                          |
| appCode               | The App Code of the user                        |
| hash                  | The unique hash for that test execution         |
| format                | The format of the results (json, json-light or html) |

If you're planning to integrate Endtest into your continuous delivery workflow, you're going to need to use both the API request for starting a test execution and the API request for fetching the results.

Because it takes time for a functional test to finish, you either need to add a `sleep` in your script or a loop that calls the API request for fetching the results at a certain interval until the test execution is finished.

Here is a sample Shell script that shows you how to do that:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
hash=$(curl -X GET --header "Accept: */*" "${3}")
for run in {1.."${4}"}
do
  sleep 30
  result=$(curl -X GET --header "Accept: */*" "https://app.endtest.io/api.php?action=getResults&appId=${1}&appCode=${2}&hash=${hash}&format=json")
  if [ "$result" == "Test is still running." ]
  then
    status=$result
    # Don't print anything
  elif [ "$result" == "Processing video recording." ]
  then
    status=$result
    # Don't print anything
  elif [ "$result" == "Stopping." ]
  then
    status=$result
  elif [ "$result" == "Erred." ]
  then
    status=$result
    echo $status
  elif [ "$result" == "" ]
  then
    status=$result
    # Don't print anything
  else
     echo "$result" | jq
     exit 0
  fi
done
exit
```

This sample script would require the following arguments:
1. The `App ID` for your account.
2. The `App Code` for your account.
3. The API Request for starting the test execution.
4. The number of times the API request for fetching the results will be sent once every 30 seconds.

For example, if you know that your test execution usually takes 3 minutes, you should use the value 7.

`7 x 30 seconds = 210 seconds > 3 minutes`

Don't forget to make your Shell script executable by running the following command:

```console
sudo chmod +x test.sh
```

And you would also need to install the `jq` package:

```sh
sudo apt-get install jq
```

The command for running the sample Shell script would have the following format:

```sh
./test.sh app-id app-code api-request-to-start-test-execution number-of-loops
```

Let's pretend we have the following values:

```
App ID = 44233559

App Code = 22381137

Endtest API Request to start test execution = "https://app.endtest.io/api.php?action=runTestSuite&appId=44233559&appCode=22381137&testSuite=106877&selectedPlatform=windows&selectedOs=a&selectedBrowser=chrome&selectedResolution=d&selectedLocation=sanfrancisco&selectedCases=all&writtenAdditionalNotes="

Number of loops = 10
```

The command for running the sample Shell script would look like this:

```sh
./test.sh 44233559 22381137 "https://app.endtest.io/api.php?action=runTestSuite&appId=44233559&appCode=22381137&testSuite=106877&selectedPlatform=windows&selectedOs=a&selectedBrowser=chrome&selectedResolution=d&selectedLocation=sanfrancisco&selectedCases=all&writtenAdditionalNotes=" 10
```

The sample script will output the Results in JSON format with the following keys:
* `test_suite_name` {`string`} - The name of the test suite.
* `configuration` {`string`} - The configuration of the machine or mobile device on which the test was executed.
* `test_cases` {`int32`} - The number of test cases.
* `passed` {`int32`} - The number of assertions that have passed.
* `failed` {`int32`} - The number of assertions that have failed.
* `errors` {`int32`} - The number of errors that have been encountered.
* `start_time` {`int32`} - The timestamp for the start of the test execution.
* `end_time` {`int32`} - The timestamp for the end of the test execution.
* `detailed_logs` {`int32`} - The detailed logs for the test execution.
* `screenshots_and_video` {`int32`} - The URL for the screenshots and the video recording of the test execution.
* `test_case_management` {`int32`} - The ID, Name, Status and External IDs for each Test Case.

 Using the `json-light` format instead of `json` means that the Results in JSON format won't include the `detailed_logs` and `screenshots_and_video` items. 

You can also use the value of the `hash` variable to generate the link to the Results page for that test execution:

```sh
results=https://app.endtest.io/results?hash="$hash"
```

>An alternative way to retrieve the results from a test execution is to add your Webhook URL in the [Webhook Notifications](https://endtest.io/docs/advanced/webhook-notifications) settings or in the Endtest API request for starting a test execution.
>
>After the test execution is finished, the results will be automatically sent to that Webhook URL.

## 4. Fetch the results for multiple test executions

The exact same Endtest API request can be used, the only difference is that you can provide multiple unique hashes, separated by commas.

This API request can only be called with an HTTP Method of type GET.

| Endtest API Parameter   | Description                 |
|-------------|-----------------------------------------|
| action      | The type of action (getResults)        |
| appId       | The App ID of the user                  |
| appCode     | The App Code of the user                |
| hash     | List of unique hashes, separated by commas    |
| format    | The format of the results (json or html)        |

>You can also fetch all the test executions by using the `getAllResults` action, which requires the following parameters: `appId`, `appCode`, `format`.

## 5. Stop a test execution

To stop a test execution with the Endtest API, use the following command:

`https://app.endtest.io/api.php?action=stopTest&appId=[your app id]&appCode=[your app code]&hash=[the returned hash]`

Replace `[your app id]` and `[your app code]` with your `appId` and `appCode` values, which you can retrieve from the [Settings](https://app.endtest.io/settings) page by clicking on the `Show API Credentials` button.

Replace `[the returned hash]` with the hash that was returned by the Endtest API request for starting a test execution.

This API request can only be called with an HTTP Method of type GET.

>You can also stop a test execution directly from the UI, by clicking on the `Stop Test` button from the Results page.
>
>You can also use the `Stop Test` option from the `Miscellaneous` action in your test. The test will automatically stop when it reaches that step.
>
>More details are available in the [How to stop a test](https://endtest.io/docs/advanced/how-to-stop-a-test/) chapter.

## 6. Get the IDs and Names of all the test suites that you have access to

To get the ids and names of all the test suites, use the following command:

`https://app.endtest.io/api.php?action=getTestSuites&appId=[your app id]&appCode=[your app code]`

Replace `[your app id]` and `[your app code]` with your `appId` and `appCode` values.

This API request can only be called with an HTTP Method of type GET.

## 7. Get the IDs, Names and External IDs of all the test cases from a test suite

To get the ids, names and external IDs of all the test cases from a test suite, use the following command:

`https://app.endtest.io/api.php?action=getTestCases&appId=[your app id]&appCode=[your app code]&testSuite=[id of the test suite]`

Replace `[your app id]` and `[your app code]` with your `appId` and `appCode` values.

Replace `[id of the test suite]` with the ID of your test suite.

You can get those values by clicking on `Get API Request` from the Run Test Suite modal.

This API request can only be called with an HTTP Method of type GET.

## 8. Upload a file in the Drive

To upload a file in the [Drive](https://app.endtest.io/drive), use the following cURL command:

`curl -X POST "https://app.endtest.io/api.php" -F "file=@/path/to/file"  -F "appId=[your app id]" -F "appCode=[your app id]" -F "visibility=[your visibility preference]"`

Replace `/path/to/file` with the local path of your file.

Replace `[your app id]` and `[your app code]` with your `appId` and `appCode` values, which you can retrieve from the [Settings](https://app.endtest.io/settings) page by clicking on the `Show API Credentials` button.

Replace `[your visibility preference]` with `OnlyMe` or `MyEntireTeam`.

This API request can only be called with an HTTP Method of type POST.

The response from this API request contains the `File Download URL` for the uploaded file.

### Endtest API Parameters for uploading a file

| Endtest API Parameter   | Description                 |
|-------------|-----------------------------------------|
| file      | The local path of the file        |
| appId       | The App ID of the user                  |
| appCode     | The App Code of the user                |
| visibility     | Visibility preference (OnlyMe or MyEntireTeam)    |
| replace    | Optional parameter. Can be used to replace existing file (True or False)  |

Sample cURL command:

`curl -X POST "https://app.endtest.io/api.php" -F "file=@/Users/matt/Desktop/calculator.ipa"  -F "appId=20112504" -F "appCode=42554172" -F "visibility=OnlyMe"`

Sample cURL response:

`https://endtest-files.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/dEREnfuqPYQRaYFWdyY7zwa0BL97lu/calculator.ipa`

[Video](https://endtest-videos.s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/documentation/endtest_api_upload_file.mp4)

 

>Only the user who uploaded the file can replace it by using the `replace` parameter.

## 9. Get the list of files uploaded in the Drive

To get the list of files from the [Drive](https://app.endtest.io/drive), use the following command:

`https://app.endtest.io/api.php?action=getFilesFromDrive&appId=[your app id]&appCode=[your app code]`

Replace `[your app id]` and `[your app code]` with your `appId` and `appCode` values.

This API request can only be called with an HTTP Method of type GET.

It will return a JSON which contains the names, the URLs and the access rules for each file.

## 10. Delete a file from the Drive

To delete a file from the [Drive](https://app.endtest.io/drive), use the following command:

`https://app.endtest.io/api.php?action=deleteFile&appId=[your app id]&appCode=[your app code]&url=[file URL]`

Replace `[your app id]` and `[your app code]` with your `appId` and `appCode` values.

Replace `[file url]` with the URL of the file from the Endtest Drive.

This API request can only be called with an HTTP Method of type GET.

>Only the user who uploaded the file can delete it with the Endtest API.

## 11. Get the number of available parallel slots

For certain complex orchestration workflows, you might need to get the number of parallel test execution slots that are currently available for your Team.

>Available Parallel Slots = Total Parallel Slots - Occupied Parallel Slots

To get that value, use the following command:

`https://app.endtest.io/api.php?action=getNumberOfAvailableParallelSlots&appId=[your app id]&appCode=[your app code]`

Replace `[your app id]` and `[your app code]` with your `appId` and `appCode` values.

This API request can only be called with an HTTP Method of type GET.

## 12. Get the list of Secure Gateway IP addresses

To get the list of Secure Gateway IP addresses, use the following command:

`https://app.endtest.io/api.php?action=getSecureGatewayIpAddresses`

This API request can only be called with an HTTP Method of type GET.

It will return a JSON with the entries that are also mentioned in the [Web Applications with restricted access](https://endtest.io/docs/web-tests/web-applications-with-restricted-access) chapter.

## 13. Import test suite from JSON file

> **Note:** This request is not available during the free trial.

If you exported a test suite from Endtest as a JSON file, you can import it back.

This API request can only be called with an HTTP Method of type GET.

Use the following command:

`https://app.endtest.io/api.php?action=importSuiteFromJSON&appId=[your app id]&appCode=[your app code]&json=[link to json file]&type=[test suite type]&suiteName=[test suite name]`

Replace `[your app id]` and `[your app code]` with your `appId` and `appCode` values.

Replace `[link to json file]` with the link to the JSON file (which can also be stored in the [Drive](https://app.endtest.io/drive)).

Replace `[test suite type]` with the type of test suite you are importing (`web` or `mobile`).

Replace `[test suite name]` with the name of the new test suite.

This API request can only be called with an HTTP Method of type GET.

The response from this API request contains the ID of the created test suite.

>Importing a test suite from a JSON file does not restore the original Settings, Collaborators, Labels, etc. It only restores the cases and the steps.
>
>The purpose of this request is only to restore a previously exported test suite.
>
>It should not be used to share a test suite with your team, since it's easier to do that by using the [Collaborators](https://endtest.io/docs/advanced/adding-collaborators) feature.
>

## 14. Import Postman collection

You can import Postman collections into Endtest, and each request gets converted to a `Send API Request` step.

### Export from Postman

1. Open the Collection you want to import into Endtest.
2. Click the `More actions (•••)` menu.
3. Choose `Export`, then select the `Collection v2.1` format when prompted.

### Upload collection

1. Upload the collection JSON file in the [Drive](https://app.endtest.io/drive).
2. Get the generated `File Download URL`.

### Import collection in a Test Case

1. Choose a Test Case from Endtest in which you want to import that collection.
2. Get the Test Case ID and Test Suite ID.
3. Use the following GET request:

`https://app.endtest.io/api.php?action=importFromPostmanCollection&appId=[your app id]&appCode=[your app code]&collection=[link to collection json file]&suite=[test suite ID]&case=[test case ID]`

Replace `[your app id]` and `[your app code]` with your `appId` and `appCode` values.

Replace `[link to collection json file]` with the `File Download URL` from the [Drive](https://app.endtest.io/drive).

Replace `[test suite ID]` with the ID of the Test Suite.

Replace `[test case ID]` with the ID of the Test Case.

## 15. Manage External IDs for Test Cases

As mentioned in the [Test Case Management](https://endtest.io/docs/advanced/importing-test-cases) chapter, you can assign External IDs to Test Cases.

You can also manage those External IDs programmatically by sending a GET request with the following format:

`https://app.endtest.io/api.php?action=manageExternalIds&operation=[operation]&testCaseId=[test case id]&externalId=[external id]&appId=[your app id]&appCode=[your app code]`

Replace `[operation]` with `assign` or `unassign`, depending on whether you want to add an External ID to a Test Case or remove it.

Replace `[test case id]` with the ID of the Test Case from Endtest.

Replace `[external id]` with the External ID of the Test Case in your Test Case Management (TCM) tool (TestRail, Zephyr, XRay, etc).

Replace `[your app id]` and `[your app code]` with your `appId` and `appCode` values, which you can retrieve from the [Settings](https://app.endtest.io/settings) page by clicking on the `Show API Credentials` button.

This API request can only be called with an HTTP Method of type GET.

| Endtest API Parameter | Description                                              |
|-----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
| action                | The type of action (`manageExternalIds`)                 |
| operation             | The type of operation (`assign` or `unassign`)           |
| testCaseId            | The ID of the test case                                  |
| externalId            | The External ID of the test case                         |
| appId                 | The App ID of the user                                   |
| appCode               | The App Code of the user                                 |

> **Note:** Assigning an External ID to a Test Case does not replace or remove the rest of the External IDs.

---

# Endtest MCP

Connect ChatGPT, Claude, Claude Code, and other MCP clients to Endtest through the Model Context Protocol to browse tests, start executions, and manage your team.

Part of the Endtest documentation (Advanced). Canonical URL: https://endtest.io/docs/advanced/endtest-mcp

---
Connect AI assistants and agentic tools to Endtest through the Model Context Protocol (MCP).

The Endtest MCP allows an MCP-compatible client to browse your Web Tests and Mobile Tests, inspect test cases and steps, view Scheduler entries and Drive files, retrieve execution results, start test executions, manage team groups and members, manage test-suite collaborators, inspect labels, and check available parallel execution capacity.

## Introduction

The Endtest MCP is available at:

```text
https://app.endtest.io/mcp
```

The recommended authentication method is OAuth. This allows supported AI assistants such as ChatGPT and Claude to connect to Endtest without requiring users to copy or expose their Endtest `App ID` and `App Code`.

When OAuth is used, the user signs in to Endtest in the browser and approves the connection. The AI client receives an OAuth access token that represents that Endtest user. The user's existing Endtest team roles, test-suite permissions, and account restrictions continue to apply.

For developer tools and MCP clients that support custom HTTP headers, the existing Endtest API credentials are also supported:

```text
X-Endtest-App-Id: YOUR_APP_ID
X-Endtest-App-Code: YOUR_APP_CODE
```

This makes the same MCP endpoint usable with OAuth-based clients as well as tools such as Claude Code and MCP Inspector.

The Endtest MCP uses Streamable HTTP.

## Connecting to the Endtest MCP

Use this MCP server URL in supported clients:

```text
https://app.endtest.io/mcp
```

For most users, OAuth is the recommended connection method.

### Connect Endtest to ChatGPT

You can connect the Endtest MCP to ChatGPT on the web when custom MCP servers are available for your ChatGPT account or workspace.

1. Open **Plugins** in ChatGPT.
2. Select the **+** button.
3. Select **Add custom MCP server** or **Create custom MCP server**.
4. Enter a name such as `Endtest`.
5. Set the Server URL to:

```text
https://app.endtest.io/mcp
```

6. Select OAuth authentication.
7. Continue with the connection.

ChatGPT discovers the Endtest OAuth configuration automatically and opens the Endtest authorization page.

If you are already signed in to Endtest, you can review the requested permissions and select **Allow**.

If you are not signed in, sign in to Endtest first and then continue the authorization flow.

After the connection is created:

1. Install the Endtest plugin from your personal or workspace Plugins section.
2. Open a new ChatGPT Work conversation.
3. Type `@` in the prompt box and select Endtest.

Example requests:

```text
List my Endtest web tests.
```

```text
Show me the test cases and steps from my Checkout Regression suite.
```

```text
How many parallel execution slots are available?
```

```text
Run my Checkout Regression test suite.
```

ChatGPT can use multiple Endtest MCP tools in the same request when a workflow requires it.

### Connect Endtest to Claude

You can connect the Endtest MCP as a custom remote connector in Claude.

1. Open **Customize** and then **Connectors**.
2. Select **Add**.
3. Select **Custom**, then **Web**.
4. Enter a name such as `Endtest`.
5. Set the remote MCP server URL to:

```text
https://app.endtest.io/mcp
```

6. Continue to the authentication settings.
7. Under **Authentication**, select **Sign in now**.
8. Under **OAuth client**, select **Use Claude's published identity**.
9. Keep **Streamable HTTP** as the transport.
10. Select **Add**.

Claude opens the Endtest authorization page.

If you are already signed in to Endtest, review the requested permissions and select **Allow**.

Once connected, enable Endtest for the Claude conversation and ask questions such as:

```text
List my Endtest web tests.
```

```text
Show me the recent failed Endtest executions.
```

```text
Find my Checkout Regression suite and explain what each test case does.
```

```text
Run my Checkout Regression suite.
```

### Connect Endtest to Claude Code

Claude Code can also connect directly using your Endtest `App ID` and `App Code`.

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http endtest https://app.endtest.io/mcp \
  --header "X-Endtest-App-Id: YOUR_APP_ID" \
  --header "X-Endtest-App-Code: YOUR_APP_CODE"
```

Then start Claude Code:

```bash
claude
```

You can then ask Claude to use your Endtest tests, results, team data, or execution tools.

Treat your `App ID` and `App Code` as secrets. Do not commit them to source control or include them in prompts.

### Testing the connection with MCP Inspector

MCP Inspector can connect using the existing Endtest API credentials.

Set the credentials as environment variables:

```bash
export ENDTEST_APP_ID='YOUR_APP_ID'
export ENDTEST_APP_CODE='YOUR_APP_CODE'
```

Then list the available tools:

```bash
npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector --cli \
  https://app.endtest.io/mcp \
  --transport http \
  --header "X-Endtest-App-Id: $ENDTEST_APP_ID" \
  --header "X-Endtest-App-Code: $ENDTEST_APP_CODE" \
  --method tools/list
```

If the connection is successful, the Endtest MCP tools will be returned.

## Available tools

The Endtest MCP currently provides the following tools.

### `list_web_tests`

Returns the Web Test suites available to the Endtest account.

The response includes information such as:

- Test suite ID.
- Test suite name.
- Project name.
- Labels.

Example:

```json
{
  "tests": [
    {
      "id": 58127403916,
      "name": "Checkout Regression - Demo Store",
      "type": "web",
      "project": "All Projects",
      "labels": [
        "Regression"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "count": 1
}
```

You can optionally search by test suite name or limit the number of returned test suites.

### `list_mobile_tests`

Returns the Mobile Test suites available to the Endtest account.

The response includes the same general information as `list_web_tests`, including the project name and labels.

Example:

```json
{
  "tests": [
    {
      "id": 48012973542,
      "name": "Android Smoke Tests - Sample App",
      "type": "mobile",
      "project": "All Projects",
      "labels": [
        "Regression"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "count": 1
}
```

### `get_test_cases`

Returns the active test cases from a Web Test or Mobile Test suite.

Required parameter:

- `test_suite_id` - The ID of the test suite.

Example request:

```json
{
  "test_suite_id": 58127403916
}
```

This tool is useful when the AI assistant needs to inspect the structure of a suite before opening a specific test case.

### `get_test_case_steps`

Returns the active steps from one test case, in execution order.

Required parameter:

- `test_case_id` - The ID of the test case.

The response contains the test case information and its steps.

A step can include fields such as:

- Step name.
- Step number.
- Action type.
- Locator.
- Parameter 1.
- Parameter 2.
- Parameter 3.
- Skip status.
- Spare locators and element information.

Example:

```json
{
  "test_case": {
    "id": 76483920155,
    "name": "Checkout Flow",
    "test_suite_id": 58127403916,
    "test_suite_name": "Checkout Regression - Demo Store"
  },
  "steps": [
    {
      "id": 59832471602,
      "step_name": "Go to URL",
      "step_number": 1,
      "type": "GoToUrl",
      "locator": "",
      "parameter1": "https://endtest-demo.io",
      "parameter2": "",
      "parameter3": ""
    }
  ],
  "step_count": 1
}
```

For security reasons, the Endtest MCP does not resolve stored AWS secret values when reading test steps.

For example, if a test uses a secret reference, the MCP returns the stored reference instead of returning the actual secret value.

### `get_test_suite_structure`

Returns the complete structure of one test suite.

This includes:

- Test suite information.
- Project name.
- Labels.
- Active test cases.
- Active test steps for every test case.

Required parameter:

- `test_suite_id` - The ID of the test suite.

Example:

```json
{
  "test_suite_id": 58127403916
}
```

The response has a structure similar to:

```json
{
  "test_suite": {
    "id": 58127403916,
    "name": "Checkout Regression - Demo Store",
    "type": "web",
    "project": "All Projects",
    "labels": [
      "Regression"
    ]
  },
  "test_cases": [
    {
      "id": 76483920147,
      "name": "Initialize Test Data",
      "position": 1,
      "step_count": 4,
      "steps": []
    },
    {
      "id": 76483920155,
      "name": "Checkout Flow",
      "position": 2,
      "step_count": 15,
      "steps": []
    }
  ],
  "test_case_count": 2,
  "step_count": 19
}
```

This tool is useful when an AI assistant needs to understand or review an entire test suite.

For large test suites, `get_test_case_steps` should be preferred when only one test case needs to be inspected, because returning an entire suite can produce a large response.

### `list_scheduler_entries`

Returns Scheduler entries visible to the Endtest account.

The tool can optionally filter entries by test suite or project and can limit the number of returned entries.

This can be useful for questions such as:

```text
Show me the scheduled executions for this test suite.
```

or:

```text
Which tests are currently scheduled to run?
```

### `list_drive_files`

Returns files available in Endtest Drive.

This includes files owned by the user and team-visible files available to that user.

You can optionally search by file name and limit the number of returned files.

Example requests to an AI assistant:

```text
Show me the CSV files in my Endtest Drive.
```

```text
Find a Drive file containing "checkout" in its name.
```

### `list_test_results`

Returns recent Endtest test executions without loading the full execution logs.

The tool can optionally filter by:

- Test suite.
- Project.
- Status.
- Number of results.

The response includes the execution hash and a link to the Results page.

Example:

```json
{
  "results": [
    {
      "hash": "Df4hiJHj5SD5wr9MK63OmeVHAODklEx0An",
      "test_suite_name": "Checkout Regression - Demo Store",
      "status": "Finished",
      "project": "All Projects",
      "result_url": "https://app.endtest.io/results?hash=Df4hiJHj5SD5wr9MK63OmeVHAODklEx0An"
    }
  ],
  "count": 1
}
```

### `get_test_result`

Returns one Endtest execution by its execution hash.

Required parameter:

- `hash` - The Endtest execution hash.

Optional parameter:

- `detail` - `light` or `full`.

The default is:

```text
light
```

Use `light` when you only need execution information such as the status, configuration, timestamps, passed and failed counts, and test case statuses.

Use `full` when the detailed JSON execution logs are also needed.

Example:

```json
{
  "hash": "Df4hiJHj5SD5wr9MK63OmeVHAODklEx0An",
  "detail": "light"
}
```

A response can contain information such as:

```json
{
  "hash": "Df4hiJHj5SD5wr9MK63OmeVHAODklEx0An",
  "test_suite_name": "Checkout Regression - Demo Store",
  "test_suite_id": 58127403916,
  "configuration": "Windows 11 Chrome Latest (v153) 1920 x 1080 San Francisco, US",
  "status": "Finished",
  "total_test_cases": 1,
  "total_passed": 1,
  "total_failed": 0,
  "errors": 0,
  "project": "All Projects",
  "result_url": "https://app.endtest.io/results?hash=Df4hiJHj5SD5wr9MK63OmeVHAODklEx0An"
}
```

### `run_web_test`

Starts an Endtest Web Test execution.

Required parameter:

- `test_suite_id` - The ID of the Web Test suite.

Optional parameters include:

- `platform`
- `os`
- `browser`
- `browser_version`
- `resolution`
- `geolocation`
- `cases`
- `notes`

If those parameters are not provided, the default configuration is:

```text
Platform: Windows
OS: Windows 11
Browser: Chrome
Browser Version: Latest
Resolution: 1920x1080
Geolocation: San Francisco
Test Cases: All
```

Example:

```json
{
  "test_suite_id": 58127403916
}
```

The tool starts the execution and returns the execution hash immediately.

Example response:

```json
{
  "started": true,
  "test_suite_id": 58127403916,
  "hashes": [
    "Df4hiJHj5SD5wr9MK63OmeVHAODklEx0An"
  ],
  "results": [
    {
      "hash": "Df4hiJHj5SD5wr9MK63OmeVHAODklEx0An",
      "result_url": "https://app.endtest.io/results?hash=Df4hiJHj5SD5wr9MK63OmeVHAODklEx0An"
    }
  ]
}
```

Executions started through the Endtest MCP are recorded in the Endtest activity logs as:

```text
Run test suite (Endtest MCP)
```

You can use `get_test_result` with the returned hash to check the execution status and results.

### `run_mobile_test`

Starts an Endtest Mobile Test execution.

Required parameters include:

- `test_suite_id`
- `platform`
- `device`
- `app`

Optional parameters include:

- `grid`
- `cases`
- `notes`

Example:

```json
{
  "test_suite_id": 48012973542,
  "platform": "android",
  "device": "DEVICE_NAME",
  "app": "APP_URL_OR_IDENTIFIER"
}
```

The tool starts the execution and returns its execution hash and Results page URL.

### `list_groups`

Returns the active groups from the current Endtest team.

Optional parameters:

- `search` - Filters groups by name.
- `limit` - Limits the number of returned groups.

Example response:

```json
{
  "team_id": 48291736,
  "groups": [
    {
      "id": 87,
      "name": "QA Engineers"
    }
  ],
  "count": 1
}
```

### `create_group`

Creates a new group in the current Endtest team.

Required parameter:

- `name` - The group name.

This action requires the Endtest team admin role.

Example:

```json
{
  "name": "Regression Team"
}
```

### `list_team_members`

Returns the active users from the current Endtest team.

The response includes information such as:

- User ID.
- Name.
- Email address.
- Blocked status.
- Whether the user is a team admin.

Optional parameters:

- `search` - Searches by name or email address.
- `limit` - Limits the number of returned users.

Use this tool before group or collaborator operations when the user ID is not already known.

### `add_team_member`

Adds a user to the current Endtest team by email address.

Required parameter:

- `email` - The email address of the user that should be added.

Example:

```json
{
  "email": "qa@example.com"
}
```

This tool uses the same Endtest team-member behavior as the Endtest UI, including the existing free-trial and paid-team limits.

If the email address does not already have an Endtest account, Endtest can create the account and send the normal invitation email.

If the user already has an Endtest account, the existing Endtest rules for team membership are applied.

### `remove_team_member`

Removes an active user from the current Endtest team.

Required parameter:

- `user_id` - The Endtest user ID.

This action requires the team admin role.

The current user cannot remove themselves with this tool.

This action uses the same removal behavior as the Endtest Team page, including deactivating the removed Endtest user according to the current team-removal implementation.

Because this is a destructive operation, an AI assistant should only call it when the user clearly requests the removal.

### `list_group_members`

Returns the active users assigned to one group.

Required parameter:

- `group_id` - The Endtest group ID.

The group must belong to the current user's team.

Example:

```json
{
  "group_id": 87
}
```

### `add_team_member_to_group`

Adds an existing team member to a group.

Required parameters:

- `group_id` - The Endtest group ID.
- `user_id` - The Endtest user ID.

This action requires the team admin role.

The user must already be an active member of the same Endtest team, and the group must belong to that team.

### `list_test_suite_collaborators`

Returns the current collaborators for one test suite.

A collaborator can be either:

- A User.
- A Group.

Each collaborator also has a role:

- `Owner`
- `Editor`
- `Viewer`

Required parameter:

- `test_suite_id` - The Endtest test suite ID.

This tool is useful before adding or removing collaborators.

### `add_collaborator`

Adds a User or Group as a collaborator to a test suite.

Required parameters:

- `test_suite_id` - The Endtest test suite ID.
- `collaborator_type` - `user` or `group`.
- `collaborator_id` - The Endtest user ID or group ID.
- `role` - `Owner`, `Editor`, or `Viewer`.

Example for a user collaborator:

```json
{
  "test_suite_id": 58127403916,
  "collaborator_type": "user",
  "collaborator_id": 91736284,
  "role": "Editor"
}
```

Example for a group collaborator:

```json
{
  "test_suite_id": 58127403916,
  "collaborator_type": "group",
  "collaborator_id": 87,
  "role": "Viewer"
}
```

The Endtest user making the request must have `Owner` access to the test suite, either directly or through a group with the `Owner` role.

User collaborators must be active members of the current team. Group collaborators must belong to the current team.

The normal Endtest collaborator notifications are used.

### `remove_collaborator`

Removes a User or Group collaborator from a test suite.

Required parameters:

- `test_suite_id` - The Endtest test suite ID.
- `collaborator_type` - `user` or `group`.
- `collaborator_id` - The Endtest user ID or group ID.

The user making the request must have `Owner` access to the test suite.

The current user cannot remove themselves as a user collaborator through this tool.

Existing Endtest safeguards also apply when removing a group that provides the current user's only Owner access.

Because this is a destructive operation, an AI assistant should only call it when the user clearly requests the removal.

### `get_available_parallel_slots`

Returns the number of parallel Endtest execution slots that are currently available.

No parameters are required.

Example response:

```json
{
  "available_parallel_slots": 3
}
```

For team accounts, the value is based on the team's configured number of parallel slots and the team's currently active executions.

For users without a team, the user's own parallel-slot configuration is used.

### `list_labels`

Returns all active labels available to the current Endtest team.

Labels are called `tags` in the Endtest backend.

The response includes:

- Label ID.
- Name.
- Description.
- Color.

Optional parameters:

- `search` - Searches labels by name.
- `limit` - Limits the number of returned labels.

### `get_test_suite_labels`

Returns the active labels assigned to one test suite.

Required parameter:

- `test_suite_id` - The Endtest test suite ID.

The labels assigned to a suite are also included in the responses from:

- `list_web_tests`
- `list_mobile_tests`
- `get_test_suite_structure`

Use `get_test_suite_labels` when only the label assignments for one suite are needed.

## Common workflows

### Find and run a Web Test

An AI assistant can first use `list_web_tests` to identify the correct suite and then use `run_web_test` to execute it.

For example, you can ask:

```text
Find my Checkout Regression test and run it on Chrome on Windows.
```

The assistant can:

1. Call `list_web_tests`.
2. Identify the matching test suite.
3. Call `run_web_test`.
4. Return the execution hash and Results page URL.

### Run a test and check the result

You can ask:

```text
Run the Checkout Regression test and tell me when it finishes.
```

The assistant can start the test with `run_web_test` and use `get_test_result` with the returned execution hash to check the result.

### Inspect one test case

You can ask:

```text
Show me the steps from the Checkout Flow test case.
```

The assistant can:

1. Find the suite with `list_web_tests`.
2. Get its test cases with `get_test_cases`.
3. Open the relevant case with `get_test_case_steps`.

### Review an entire test suite

You can ask:

```text
Show me the complete structure of the Checkout Regression test suite.
```

or:

```text
Review this test suite and explain what each test case is doing.
```

The assistant can use `get_test_suite_structure` to retrieve the complete hierarchy:

```text
Test Suite
  -> Test Cases
      -> Test Steps
```

### Review recent failures

You can ask:

```text
Show me the recent failed executions for this test suite.
```

The assistant can use `list_test_results` to find the relevant execution and `get_test_result` to inspect it in more detail.

### Manage a group

You can ask:

```text
Create a group called Regression Team and add Alice to it.
```

The assistant can:

1. Call `list_team_members` to identify Alice's user ID.
2. Call `create_group`.
3. Call `list_groups` to identify the new group ID if needed.
4. Call `add_team_member_to_group`.

The group-management write actions require the Endtest team admin role.

### Add a test suite collaborator

You can ask:

```text
Give the Regression Team group Editor access to the Checkout test suite.
```

The assistant can:

1. Find the test suite with `list_web_tests` or `list_mobile_tests`.
2. Find the group with `list_groups`.
3. Call `add_collaborator` with `collaborator_type` set to `group`.

### Check execution capacity

You can ask:

```text
How many parallel test slots do we have available right now?
```

The assistant can call `get_available_parallel_slots`.

### Inspect labels

You can ask:

```text
Show me all of our labels and tell me which labels are assigned to the Checkout suite.
```

The assistant can use `list_labels` and `get_test_suite_labels`.

## Authentication and security

The Endtest MCP supports two authentication methods.

### OAuth

OAuth is the recommended method for user-facing AI clients such as ChatGPT and Claude.

With OAuth:

1. The client discovers Endtest's OAuth configuration.
2. The user signs in to Endtest.
3. Endtest shows the permissions requested by the connection.
4. The user approves or declines the connection.
5. The client receives an OAuth token associated with that Endtest user.

The user's Endtest password, `App ID`, and `App Code` are not exposed to ChatGPT or Claude through this flow.

The Endtest MCP currently defines these OAuth permission scopes:

- `endtest.read` - Read tests, test cases, steps, results, Drive files, Scheduler entries, team information, groups, collaborators, labels, and execution capacity.
- `endtest.execute` - Start Web Test and Mobile Test executions.
- `endtest.manage` - Manage team members, groups, group membership, and test-suite collaborators when the Endtest user's role allows it.

OAuth permissions do not override Endtest permissions.

For example:

- A non-admin team member cannot remove another team member simply because the client has `endtest.manage`.
- A user without Owner access to a test suite cannot change that suite's collaborators.
- A user can only access tests and results that their Endtest account is allowed to access.

### App ID and App Code

For developer tools and MCP clients that support custom request headers, Endtest also accepts the same credentials used by the Endtest API:

```text
X-Endtest-App-Id
X-Endtest-App-Code
```

These credentials determine the Endtest user for the MCP session.

Store the `App ID` and `App Code` securely and do not include them directly in prompts, screenshots, source code, or public configuration files.

OAuth is generally preferable for end users because it does not require copying these credentials into another application.

### Stored secrets

When test steps reference stored secrets, the Endtest MCP returns the secret reference but does not resolve and expose the stored secret value.

### Permission checks

Team-admin and test-suite permission checks are enforced for MCP management actions.

Creating groups, adding users to groups, and removing team members follow the existing Endtest team-role rules.

Collaborator changes require Owner access to the test suite.

Destructive tools such as `remove_team_member` and `remove_collaborator` should only be used after the user has clearly requested the change.

## Notes

The Endtest MCP endpoint is:

```text
https://app.endtest.io/mcp
```

The endpoint supports OAuth for clients such as ChatGPT and Claude and also supports `X-Endtest-App-Id` and `X-Endtest-App-Code` headers for compatible developer tools.

The MCP currently supports reading tests, test cases, test steps, complete test suite structures, Scheduler entries, Drive files, test results, team members, groups, collaborators, labels, and available parallel slots.

It also supports starting Web Test and Mobile Test executions, creating groups, adding team members, assigning users to groups, adding and removing test-suite collaborators, and removing team members when the current user has the required permissions.

Additional Endtest functionality can be added to the MCP over time without changing the existing tool workflows.

# Adding Collaborators

Invite collaborators to your Endtest tests. Share suites with engineers, QA, and stakeholders with granular per-test or project-level permissions.

## Steps

If you have the Owner role, you can revoke access by clicking on the `X` button next to a user.

## Collaborators FAQ

#### 1. Why is the `Users` dropdown empty?

The `Users` dropdown is populated with the users from your `Team`.

If the `Users` dropdown is empty, it either means that you do not have other users in your team or every user in your team has already been added as a Collaborator.

#### 2. How do I add `users` in my team?

If you are a Team Admin, you can add users in your in the Team section from the [Settings](https://app.endtest.io/settings) page.

More details about adding users in your team are available in the [Team](https://endtest.io/docs/advanced/team) chapter.

#### 3. Why is the `Groups` dropdown empty?

The `Groups` dropdown is populated with the groups from your `Team`.

If the `Groups` dropdown is empty, it either means that you do not have groups in your team or every group in your team has already been added as a Collaborator.

#### 4. How do I add `groups`?

If you are a Team Admin, you can create groups in the Team section from the [Settings](https://app.endtest.io/settings) page.

More details about creating groups in your team are available in the [Team](https://endtest.io/docs/advanced/team) chapter.

#### 5. What happens if a `user` is added as a `Viewer` but that `user` is also part of a `group` which is added as an `Owner` or `Editor`?

In all situations where a `user` has access to a test through different roles, the highest role will override the other roles.

In this case, the `user` will have `Owner` permissions, since the `user` is part of a group which is added with the `Owner` role.

#### 6. Can I remove myself or my `group` from the `Collaborators` list for a test suite?

No, you cannot remove yourself from the `Collaborators` list, even if you have the `Owner` role.

The only solution in this situation is to be removed by another `Owner`.

If you are part of a `group`, you cannot remove that `group` from the `Collaborators` list.

# Visual AI

Add Visual AI steps to Endtest tests to detect UI regressions automatically. Compare screenshots intelligently and flag meaningful visual changes only.

Part of the Endtest documentation (Advanced). Canonical URL: https://endtest.io/docs/advanced/visual-ai

---
## Introduction

You can use the Visual AI capabilities of our platform to ensure every part of the UI is tested.

If something changes on the screen, you will be alerted in the test results.

This method is also known as Visual Testing or Screenshot Comparison.

You can visually verify your entire page or only certain elements.

[Video](https://endtest-videos.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/documentation/endtest_visual_testing_feature.mp4)

## Guide

You can use one of these 3 options:
1. Page Matches Screenshot
2. Full Page Matches Screenshot
3. Element Matches Screenshot

The difference between `Page Matches Screenshot` and `Full Page Matches Screenshot` is that the first option refers to the viewport, while the second option refers to entire DOM.

You can find those options in:

- `Add Assertion` → `Visual Assertion`
- `Start IF Statement` → `Visual Condition`

You must provide a `Baseline Screenshot URL` for those options.

How to obtain a `Baseline Screenshot URL`:
1. Add a `Take Screenshot`, `Snipping Tool` or `Generate Full Page Screenshot` step in your test.
2. Execute the test.
3. Get the URL of the screenshot from the Results section.

If the screenshots have different sizes, the larger one will be automatically resized to match the smaller one.

The logs will display the baseline screenshot, the current screenshot and a third screenshot that highlights the visual differences:

![](https://app.endtest.io/images/screenshot-comparison.png)

>Each Visual AI step will also have an `Accept New Baseline` button in the Results section.
>That action will update the Baseline Screenshot from that step with the Current Screenshot.

## Excluding Elements

You can exclude specific elements from a Visual AI comparison by providing a comma-separated list of CSS Selectors.

This is useful for parts of the page that change between executions and should be ignored, such as timestamps, ads, or carousels.

For example:

```
.cookie-banner, #live-chat, .ad-slot
```

Anything matching those selectors will be excluded from the screenshot comparison.

## What is the Visual Tolerance?

The `Visual Tolerance (%)` from the `Advanced Settings` can be configured to manage the relationship between the percentage result and the assertion result.

For example, if you select 5%, your assertion will fail if the difference between the screenshots is more than 5%.

The `Visual Tolerance (%)` doesn't influence the precision of the screenshot comparison and the percentage result.

It only determines the percentage at which the assertion will be marked as Passed or Failed.

## What is the Visual Fuzz?

The `Visual Fuzz (%)` from the `Advanced Settings` can be configured to set the precision of the screenshot comparison.

A smaller value will lead to a more precise screenshot comparison.

A higher value will lead to a less precise screenshot comparison.

An optimal value for the `Visual Fuzz (%)` is somewhere between 2% and 20%, but you can select values between 1% and 50%.

>The Full Page Screenshot option is only available for Web Tests.
>
>Since the webdrivers only allow you to take a screenshot of the visible viewport, the Full Page Screenshots are generated by taking multiple screenshots and stitching them together.
>
>This may cause some elements with the CSS property **position: fixed** to be displayed multiple times.
>
>If you're testing in multiple browsers and resolutions, we recommend having baseline screenshots for each combination.
>
>You can manage those combinations by using [If Statements](https://endtest.io/docs/web-tests/if-statements-for-web-tests/) and [System Variables](https://endtest.io/docs/advanced/how-to-use-variables/#system-variables).

# Test Case Version History

Track changes to your Endtest test cases over time. Compare versions, review edits, and restore an earlier version of a Web or Mobile test.

Part of the Endtest documentation (Advanced). Canonical URL: https://endtest.io/docs/advanced/test-case-version-history

---
Test Case Version History keeps a record of the changes made to a test case over time.

Each time a test case is saved, Endtest creates a new version containing the steps and configuration that existed at that moment. You can compare two versions, review the changes, and restore an older version when needed.

Version History is available for both **Web Tests** and **Mobile Tests**.

## Open the Version History

1. Open **Web Tests** or **Mobile Tests**.
2. Open the test suite that contains the test case.
3. Locate the test case in the list.
4. Click the **History** button next to that test case.

The History button is displayed next to the other test case actions, before **Delete**.

Version History belongs to the entire test case. It tracks changes made to the steps inside that test case.

## View the Available Versions

The left side of the Version History window shows the versions that are available for the selected test case.

Each version can include:

- The version number.
- The date and time when it was created.
- The user who created it.
- The number of steps in that version.
- The source of the change, such as a manual save or a restore.
- An optional change message.
- An indication of which version is currently active.

The newest version is normally shown first.

## Compare Two Versions

Use the **From** and **To** selectors to choose the versions you want to compare.

For example:

- **From:** Version 2
- **To:** Version 5

Select **Compare** to display the differences.

The comparison is based on the logical identity of each step, not only its database row or current position. This allows Endtest to recognize the same step across multiple saves, even when the step was edited or moved.

## Change Types

The comparison can classify a step as:

### Modified

The step exists in both versions, but one or more of its values changed.

Examples include:

- A URL was changed.
- A locator was changed.
- The text entered by a step was changed.
- An assertion value was changed.
- An API request configuration was edited.
- A variable value was changed.

Changed values are highlighted in the comparison.

### Added

The step exists in the newer version but not in the older version.

### Deleted

The step exists in the older version but not in the newer version.

### Moved

The step exists in both versions, but its relative position in the test case changed.

Adding another step above an existing step does not automatically mean that the existing step was moved. Endtest uses the relative order of the steps to distinguish an actual move from a normal position shift caused by an insertion or deletion.

### Unchanged

The step exists in both versions with the same content and relative order.

## Read the Step Comparison

The comparison presents each step in a readable format instead of showing the raw stored data.

Depending on the action, the comparison can display information such as:

- Step number.
- Action.
- Step name.
- URL.
- Target element.
- Locator type and locator value.
- Text or value.
- Variable name.
- Assertion details.
- Additional action-specific values.
- Whether the step is skipped.
- Backup locators used for self-healing.

Empty values and internal placeholder values are hidden when they do not provide useful information.

## Restore an Older Version

To restore a previous version:

1. Open Version History.
2. Locate the version you want to restore.
3. Select **Restore**.
4. Confirm the action.

Restoring a version does not delete the newer versions.

Instead, Endtest creates a new version whose contents are copied from the selected historical version. This preserves the complete audit trail and allows the restore itself to be reviewed or reversed later.

For example:

```text
Version 5 — Current version
Version 4
Version 3 — Version selected for restore
Version 2
Version 1
```

After restoring Version 3:

```text
Version 6 — Restored from Version 3
Version 5
Version 4
Version 3
Version 2
Version 1
```

Version 6 becomes the current version, while the previous versions remain available.

## What Is Restored

A restore recreates the test case steps from the selected version, including their:

- Order.
- Action types.
- Step names.
- Locators.
- Parameters and values.
- Skip settings.
- Backup locators.
- Other stored step configuration.

The restored steps receive new internal database rows, while their logical step identities are preserved. This allows future comparisons to recognize them as the same steps.

## Concurrent Changes

Endtest can detect when the test case was changed after a user opened it.

When version conflict protection is available, a save or restore based on an outdated version can be rejected instead of silently overwriting newer work.

Reload the test case and review the latest version before saving again.

## Permissions

Version History follows the same access rules as the test case.

Users who can view the test case can review its available versions. Restoring a version requires permission to modify that test case.

## Recommended Practices

Review Version History when:

- A test starts failing after a recent edit.
- A locator or assertion was changed unexpectedly.
- A large test case was reorganized.
- Several users work on the same test.
- You need to understand when a configuration changed.
- You need to return to a previously working version.

For important changes, add a short change message when that option is available. A useful message explains why the test was changed rather than only describing what was changed.

Example:

```text
Updated checkout assertions for the redesigned order confirmation page.
```

## Important Notes

- Version History is tracked per test case, not per test suite.
- Saving a test case creates a new version.
- Restoring an older version creates another new version.
- Existing historical versions are not overwritten.
- The current version is clearly marked in the version list.
- Deleted steps remain visible when comparing with a version in which they existed.

# Data-driven Testing

Run the same Endtest test against hundreds of data rows from CSV or Excel, perfect for form validation, search permutations, and edge-case sweeps.

Part of the Endtest documentation (Advanced). Canonical URL: https://endtest.io/docs/advanced/data-driven-testing

---
## Introduction

The `Import Test Case Multiple Times (CSV)` action allows you to execute the same test case multiple times in a row, while extracting data from a CSV file.

## Guide

When you select the `Import Test Case Multiple Times (CSV)` action, the `Test case to import` dropdown gets populated with the entire list of test cases that you have access to.

In order to get a `CSV File URL`, you can upload your CSV file in our [Drive](https://app.endtest.io/drive) section.

For each row of the CSV file, a new set of variables will be created.

The name of the variables will be generated from the Column Headers of the CSV file, all spaces and non-alphanumeric characters will be removed and a `$` will be prepended to the name of the variable.

Here are some  examples:

```csv
| Column Header in CSV file | Generated Variable Name |
|---------------------------|-------------------------|
| email                     | $email                  |
| User Name                 | $UserName               |
| The_Address               | $TheAddress             |
| zip-code                  | $zipcode                |
```

The data from the rest of the CSV rows will not be altered in any way.

Let's suppose we have the following CSV file:

```csv
| email             | password           |
|-------------------|--------------------|
| jimmy@example.com | ^^VT[Nv20zSwCBh4*  |
| walter@random.com | ^]LNf]CHNQKOX(g*ld |
| jessica@inbox.com | ba!^tBJ            |
```

We can see that the CSV file has 2 column and 4 rows.

The Column Headers will be used only to name the variables.

The values for those variables will be extracted from the rest of the 3 rows.

If we would use this CSV file in our test with the `Import Test Case Multiple Times (CSV)` action, the imported test case would be executed 3 times, with 3 sets of variables, one set from each row.

You can only import test cases from other Web Tests in a Web Test.

You can only import test cases from other Mobile Tests in a Mobile Test.

When the test is executed, the `Import Test Case Multiple Times (CSV)` action executes the latest version of the imported test case.

The variables declared in the imported test case can be accessed from the test suite in which it gets imported.

[Video](https://endtest-videos.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/documentation/endtest_data_driven_testing_csv.mp4)

 

 You can also extract data from Google Sheets by using the `Google Sheets API` and the [Send API Request](https://endtest.io/docs/advanced/send-api-requests) action from Endtest.

# API Testing: Send API Requests

API Testing in Endtest: how to send API requests, validate responses, and chain calls in your test cases

Part of the Endtest documentation (Advanced). Canonical URL: https://endtest.io/docs/advanced/send-api-requests

---
## Introduction

Endtest supports **API Testing**. You can send API requests, validate responses, and chain multiple API calls together as part of any Web Test or Mobile Test.

The `Send API Request` action is how API Testing works in Endtest. You can call REST APIs, send JSON bodies, attach files, set custom headers and authorization, and assert against the response status, body, headers, or cookies.

API Testing in Endtest can be used on its own or alongside UI testing. The same test case can drive a browser, hit your API, and verify both behave correctly.

## Structure

The following HTTP request methods are available:
* GET
* POST
* PUT
* DELETE
* HEAD
* PATCH

The `Send API Request` modal has 5 tabs:
1. Params
2. Authorization
3. Headers
4. Body
5. Response

The `Response` tab has 5 sections:
1. Status
2. Body
3. Cookies
4. Headers
5. Duration

The `Send` button allows you to test the API request and see the output in the `Response` section.

Since this preview is done in the frontend, the API request will be sent with AJAX.

But when you actually execute that test, the API request will be sent with Python.

This means that the `Send API Request` action will work for both Web Tests and Mobile Tests.

[Video](https://endtest-videos.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/documentation/endtest_send_api_request.mp4)

## Adding variables

You can use variables in the API Request.

Simply typing `$` inside an input will display a dropdown with the available variables.

You can concatenate variables with strings or with other variables by placing the variable name between double curly brackets: 
`My name is {{$username}} and my email is {{$email}}`

You can also store the output from the `Response` section in variables, by using the `Store in variable` option.

This allows you to chain requests and pass values from one `Send API Request` step to another.

If you need to extract values from JSON objects or arrays, you can use the actions from the [Endtest Utilities](https://endtest.io/docs/advanced/utilities/).

Since the variables are created only when you execute the test, they won't be available when you test the API request by clicking on the `Send` button. 

## Sessions and Cookies

If you have multiple `Send API Request` steps in a test execution, the requests will use the same session.

That means the cookies generated by a `Send API Request` step will be automatically included in the next `Send API Request` steps from that test execution.

In case you want to clear the session, you can use the `Clear API Session` method from the `Miscellaneous` action.

>The session and cookies from the `Send API Request` steps are separate from the session and cookies from the browsers and mobile apps.
>
>The API requests are not sent through the browsers or the mobile apps.
>
>Cookies generated by `Send API Request` steps will not be automatically placed in the browser, but you can transfer them to variables and place them in the browser with [Execute JavaScript](https://endtest.io/docs/web-tests/execute-javascript) steps.
>

## Sending files

You can also send a file with a `Send API Request` step.

The file download link must be added in the `Value` cell.

A variable containing that file download link can also be used.

Files can be stored in the [Endtest Drive](https://endtest.io/docs/advanced/drive), but you can also use other file storage systems.

The `Description` for that row must be `file`, otherwise the test won't know that it needs to download the file and place it in the request.

Here's an example for sending a file to our own [Endtest API](https://endtest.io/docs/advanced/how-to-use-the-endtest-api):

![](https://app.endtest.io/images/send_file_in_send_api_request.jpg)

If the `Description` does not have the value `file`, the row will be processed as having a file download link, and not a file. 

## Common errors and solutions

### 1. Missing Headers

In some situations, the endpoint that you are calling expects certain headers.

If your API request isn't getting the expected response, add the following items in the `Headers` section:

| Key           | Value                    |
|---------------|--------------------------|
| Content-Type  | application/vnd.api+json |
| Cache-Control | no-cache                 |
| User-Agent    | Endtest                  |

>When you click on the `Send` button, the API request is sent through your browser. This might cause certain headers (such as the `User-Agent`) to be overwritten by your browser.
>
>When you execute the test, the API request is sent by a Python script from the machine on which the test is being executed. This means that no headers will be overwritten.
>
>If you're not getting the expected response when you click on the `Send` button, try to execute the test and see if that gives you the expected response.

### 2. Restricted Access

When you execute a test which contains a `Send API Request` step, the API request will be sent from one of our IP addresses.

If you're getting a HTTP status code like 404 (Not Found) or 403 (Forbidden), check if you need to whitelist our list of Secure Gateway IP addresses:

| Secure Gateway IP Addresses |
|-----------------------------|
| 34.211.40.72                |
| 35.166.159.89               |
| 207.254.40.71               |
| 207.254.60.102              |
| 52.89.18.176                |
| 52.26.12.35                 |
| 54.187.169.42               |
| 52.43.87.222                |
| 34.214.85.4                 |
| 54.184.162.15               |
| 44.237.178.201              |
| 44.238.105.245              |
| 44.228.22.115               |
| 35.81.185.74                |
| 207.254.52.64               |
| 44.241.213.227              |
| 52.26.206.66                |
| 52.13.40.64                 |
| 44.238.190.158              |
| 207.254.60.6                |
| 207.254.41.137              |
| 207.254.60.76               |
| 34.213.62.124               |
| 54.191.53.140               |
| 18.237.140.182              |

### 3. No response in the Results

When you execute a test which contains a `Send API Request` step, the test execution logs will only contain the `Status` and the `Body` from the response if you selected the `Store in variable` action in the `Response` tab from the `Send API Request` modal.

### 4. Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) errors

Browsers use CORS in APIs such as XMLHttpRequest or Fetch to mitigate the risks of cross-origin HTTP requests.

When you click on the `Send` button from the `Send API Request` modal, the API request is sent through your own browser.

That means you might encounter CORS errors when doing that.

But when you run the test, the API request doesn't go through the browser, that means that you won't encounter CORS errors when running the test.
