# Jenkins

Run Endtest end-to-end tests from a Jenkins Pipeline with the official Endtest plugin.

Part of the Endtest documentation (Integrations). Canonical URL: https://endtest.io/docs/integrations/jenkins

---
## Overview

The Endtest Jenkins plugin lets you start Endtest automated tests directly from a Jenkins Pipeline, wait for the executions to finish, and use the results in later Pipeline steps.

The plugin supports:

- Secure storage of Endtest API credentials in Jenkins
- Single Endtest executions
- Multiple executions started by the same API request
- Label-based Endtest API requests
- Automatic polling until execution results are available
- Aggregate results across multiple executions
- Optional Jenkins build failure when Endtest reports failures or errors
- Resuming result polling after a Jenkins controller restart
- `json` and `json-light` result formats

## Requirements

Before configuring the integration, make sure you have:

- Jenkins 2.528.3 or newer
- Permission to install Jenkins plugins and create credentials
- An Endtest account
- An Endtest App ID and App Code
- An Endtest API request that starts the test suite, configuration, or label you want to run

For more information about creating an API request, see [How to use the Endtest API](https://endtest.io/docs/advanced/how-to-use-the-endtest-api).

## Install the Endtest plugin

1. In Jenkins, open **Manage Jenkins**.
2. Select **Plugins**.
3. Open the **Available plugins** tab.
4. Search for **Endtest**.
5. Select the Endtest plugin and install it.
6. Restart Jenkins if your Jenkins installation asks you to do so.

The plugin page is available at:

[https://plugins.jenkins.io/endtest/](https://plugins.jenkins.io/endtest/)

## Add Endtest credentials to Jenkins

Storing the App ID and App Code in Jenkins Credentials is recommended. This keeps the credentials out of the Jenkinsfile and allows the same credential entry to be reused by multiple jobs.

1. In Jenkins, open **Manage Jenkins**.
2. Select **Credentials**.
3. Open the credential store and domain where the Pipeline should have access.
4. Select **Add Credentials**.
5. For **Kind**, select **Endtest API credentials**.
6. Enter the following values:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| App ID | Your Endtest App ID |
| App Code | Your Endtest App Code |
| ID | A Jenkins credential ID, such as `endtest-api` |
| Description | An optional description for the credential |

The examples in this guide use the credential ID `endtest-api`.

> The Jenkins credential ID is not the Endtest App ID. It is the identifier Jenkins uses to locate the stored credential.

## Prepare the Endtest API request

Create or copy an Endtest API request for the test suite, configuration, or label you want Jenkins to execute.

The request must:

- Use HTTPS
- Use the `app.endtest.io` host
- Start an Endtest execution
- Include all execution settings required by your Endtest project

A request may contain `appId` and `appCode`, but storing those values in Jenkins Credentials is safer. When a credential ID is provided, the plugin automatically adds any missing `appId` or `appCode` values to the request.

When credentials are present both in the API request and in Jenkins Credentials, the values in the API request take precedence.

## Add Endtest to a Jenkins Pipeline

The plugin provides the Pipeline step:

```groovy
endtestRun(...)
```

A basic Declarative Pipeline example looks like this:

```groovy
pipeline {
    agent any

    stages {
        stage('Run Endtest') {
            steps {
                script {
                    def result = endtestRun(
                        credentialsId: 'endtest-api',
                        apiRequest: 'https://app.endtest.io/api.php?<YOUR_ENDTEST_API_PARAMETERS>'
                    )

                    echo "Executions: ${result.executionCount}"
                    echo "Test cases: ${result.testCases}"
                    echo "Passed: ${result.passed}"
                    echo "Failed: ${result.failed}"
                    echo "Errors: ${result.errors}"
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

Replace the value of `apiRequest` with the API request generated for your Endtest tests.

By default, the plugin:

- Waits for up to 30 minutes
- Checks the Endtest results every 30 seconds
- Uses the `json-light` results format
- Fails the Jenkins build when Endtest reports failed assertions or errors

## Complete Pipeline example

The following example displays aggregate results and a link to each Endtest execution:

```groovy
pipeline {
    agent any

    stages {
        stage('Run Endtest') {
            steps {
                script {
                    def result = endtestRun(
                        credentialsId: 'endtest-api',
                        apiRequest: 'https://app.endtest.io/api.php?<YOUR_ENDTEST_API_PARAMETERS>',
                        timeoutMinutes: 45,
                        pollIntervalSeconds: 30,
                        failBuild: true,
                        resultsFormat: 'json-light'
                    )

                    echo "Endtest completed ${result.executionCount} execution(s)"
                    echo "Test cases: ${result.testCases}"
                    echo "Passed: ${result.passed}"
                    echo "Failed: ${result.failed}"
                    echo "Errors: ${result.errors}"

                    result.executions.eachWithIndex { execution, index ->
                        echo "Execution ${index + 1}"
                        echo "Test suite: ${execution.testSuiteName}"
                        echo "Configuration: ${execution.configuration}"
                        echo "Hash: ${execution.hash}"
                        echo "Results: ${execution.resultsUrl}"
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

## Pipeline parameters

| Parameter | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `apiRequest` | Yes | None | The Endtest API request used to start one or more executions |
| `credentialsId` | Conditional | None | The ID of an **Endtest API credentials** entry stored in Jenkins |
| `timeoutMinutes` | No | `30` | Maximum number of minutes Jenkins waits for the results |
| `pollIntervalSeconds` | No | `30` | Number of seconds between result checks |
| `failBuild` | No | `true` | Fails the Pipeline when Endtest reports failures or errors |
| `resultsFormat` | No | `json-light` | Endtest result format, either `json` or `json-light` |

### Parameter limits

- `timeoutMinutes` must be between `1` and `1440`.
- `pollIntervalSeconds` must be between `5` and `300`.
- `resultsFormat` must be `json` or `json-light`.
- `credentialsId` is optional only when both `appId` and `appCode` are already included in `apiRequest`.

## Control the Jenkins build result manually

When `failBuild` is set to `true`, the plugin stops the Pipeline step with an error when Endtest reports one or more failed assertions or errors.

Set `failBuild` to `false` when you want the Pipeline to inspect the results and decide what to do:

```groovy
script {
    def result = endtestRun(
        credentialsId: 'endtest-api',
        apiRequest: 'https://app.endtest.io/api.php?<YOUR_ENDTEST_API_PARAMETERS>',
        failBuild: false
    )

    if (result.errors > 0) {
        error("Endtest reported ${result.errors} execution errors")
    }

    if (result.failed > 0) {
        unstable("Endtest reported ${result.failed} failed assertions")
    }
}
```

This is useful when failed tests should mark a build as unstable instead of immediately failing it.

## Run multiple Endtest executions

A single Endtest API request can start more than one execution. For example, an API request that runs a label may start multiple test suites or configurations.

When Endtest returns multiple execution hashes, the plugin automatically:

- Stores every execution hash
- Polls all executions
- Waits until all results are available
- Returns the result of each execution
- Calculates aggregate totals
- Exposes a results URL for each execution

No Jenkinsfile changes are required to support multiple executions.

You can check whether the request started multiple executions using:

```groovy
if (result.multipleExecutions) {
    echo "The Endtest request started ${result.executionCount} executions"
}
```

## Returned result

The `endtestRun` step returns a map that can be used by later Pipeline logic.

### Aggregate fields

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `executionCount` | Number of Endtest executions started by the request |
| `hashes` | List of Endtest execution hashes |
| `executions` | List containing the result of each execution |
| `resultsUrls` | List of links to the Endtest Results pages |
| `testCases` | Total number of test cases |
| `passed` | Total number of passed assertions |
| `failed` | Total number of failed assertions |
| `errors` | Total number of errors |
| `multipleExecutions` | `true` when the request started more than one execution |

### Fields for each execution

Each item in `result.executions` can contain:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `testSuiteName` | Name of the Endtest test suite |
| `configuration` | Endtest execution configuration |
| `testCases` | Number of test cases |
| `passed` | Number of passed assertions |
| `failed` | Number of failed assertions |
| `errors` | Number of errors |
| `startTime` | Execution start time |
| `endTime` | Execution end time |
| `hash` | Endtest execution hash |
| `resultsUrl` | Link to the execution in Endtest |
| `detailedLogs` | Detailed execution log data when included in the selected result format |
| `screenshotsAndVideo` | Screenshot and video data when available |
| `testCaseManagement` | Test case management data when available |

For a single execution, the plugin also exposes the individual execution fields directly on the returned result. For example:

```groovy
echo "Test suite: ${result.testSuiteName}"
echo "Results: ${result.resultsUrl}"
```

## Use credentials already included in the API request

For compatibility with existing Jenkinsfiles, the plugin also accepts an API request that already contains `appId` and `appCode`:

```groovy
endtestRun(
    apiRequest: 'https://app.endtest.io/api.php?<PARAMETERS>&appId=<APP_ID>&appCode=<APP_CODE>'
)
```

This works without `credentialsId`, but it is not recommended because the credentials become part of the Jenkinsfile and may be exposed through source control, build configuration, or logs.

Prefer Jenkins Credentials whenever possible.

## Jenkins restart behavior

After Endtest returns the execution hashes, the plugin stores its polling state in Jenkins. If the Jenkins controller restarts while the tests are running, result polling resumes after Jenkins comes back online.

If Jenkins restarts while the initial request is still being sent and no execution hash has been received yet, the step fails safely instead of repeating the start request. This prevents the plugin from accidentally starting the same Endtest tests twice.

In that situation:

1. Check Endtest to see whether an execution was created.
2. Review the Jenkins console output.
3. Start the Pipeline again when appropriate.

## Console output

The plugin writes status information to the Jenkins build log, including:

- When the Endtest request starts
- The number of executions started
- Each execution hash
- A results link for each execution
- Current Endtest execution status
- Final totals for passed, failed, and errored assertions

Sensitive Jenkins credential values are not intentionally printed by the plugin.

## Troubleshooting

### `credentialsId is required when appId or appCode is missing from apiRequest`

The API request does not contain complete credentials and no Jenkins credential ID was provided.

Add `credentialsId` to the Pipeline step:

```groovy
credentialsId: 'endtest-api'
```

Make sure the referenced Jenkins credential is of the type **Endtest API credentials**.

### `Could not find Endtest credentials with ID`

Jenkins could not find an Endtest credential matching the provided ID.

Check:

- The credential ID for spelling differences
- The credential scope
- The credential domain
- Whether the Pipeline job has permission to access it

### `The Endtest API request must use HTTPS`

The value of `apiRequest` starts with `http://` or does not contain a valid scheme.

Use an HTTPS API request generated by Endtest.

### `The Endtest API request must use the app.endtest.io host`

The plugin only accepts API requests sent to `app.endtest.io`.

Check that the request was copied correctly and was not replaced with a proxy, shortened URL, or different host.

### `Timed out waiting for Endtest`

The execution did not finish before `timeoutMinutes` was reached.

Increase the timeout for longer test suites:

```groovy
timeoutMinutes: 60
```

Also check the Endtest Results page to determine whether the execution is still running or encountered a problem.

### Jenkins build failed after the Endtest execution completed

With the default `failBuild: true` setting, the Jenkins build fails when Endtest reports failed assertions or execution errors.

Use `failBuild: false` when you want to handle those results yourself.

### Endtest returned an HTTP or invalid response error

Check:

- The App ID and App Code
- The API request parameters
- Network access from the Jenkins controller to `https://app.endtest.io`
- Whether the Endtest service is reachable
- Whether the request works when used directly according to the Endtest API documentation

## Security recommendations

- Store the App Code in Jenkins Credentials.
- Do not commit `appId` and `appCode` values to source control.
- Restrict access to the Jenkins credential domain.
- Use a dedicated Endtest API credential for CI/CD when appropriate.
- Rotate the App Code if it is exposed.
- Avoid printing the full authenticated API request in Pipeline logs.

## Additional resources

- [Endtest API documentation](https://endtest.io/docs/advanced/how-to-use-the-endtest-api)
- [Endtest Jenkins plugin](https://plugins.jenkins.io/endtest/)
- [Endtest Jenkins plugin source code](https://github.com/jenkinsci/endtest-plugin)

---

# GitHub

Integrating Endtest with GitHub

Part of the Endtest documentation (Integrations). Canonical URL: https://endtest.io/docs/integrations/github

---
## Instructions

You can use our [Endtest GitHub Action](https://github.com/marketplace/actions/run-endtest-functional-tests) to trigger Endtest tests from a GitHub Actions workflow and wait for the results.

The action supports:

* Running a single Endtest test suite
* Running multiple test suites using an Endtest label
* Waiting for every triggered execution to finish
* Returning individual and aggregated execution results
* Failing the GitHub Actions job when tests fail
* The `json` and `json-light` result formats

Your Endtest App ID and App Code are available on the [Endtest Settings page](https://app.endtest.io/settings).

We recommend storing them as GitHub Actions secrets named:

* `ENDTEST_APP_ID`
* `ENDTEST_APP_CODE`

### Example workflow

The following example runs every Endtest test suite with the `Critical` label:

```yaml
name: Run Endtest tests

on:
  push:
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  endtest:
    name: Endtest functional tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Run Endtest tests
        id: endtest
        uses: endtest-technologies/github-run-tests-action@v1.10
        with:
          app_id: ${{ secrets.ENDTEST_APP_ID }}
          app_code: ${{ secrets.ENDTEST_APP_CODE }}
          api_request: >-
            https://app.endtest.io/api.php?action=runWeb&appId=${{ secrets.ENDTEST_APP_ID }}&appCode=${{ secrets.ENDTEST_APP_CODE }}&label=Critical&platform=windows&os=windows11&browser=chrome&browserVersion=latest&resolution=1280x1024&geolocation=sanfrancisco&cases=all&notes=
          number_of_loops: 60
          results_format: json-light
          fail_build: true

      - name: Show Endtest results
        if: always()
        env:
          EXECUTION_COUNT: ${{ steps.endtest.outputs.execution_count }}
          TEST_SUITE_NAMES: ${{ steps.endtest.outputs.test_suite_name }}
          TEST_CASES: ${{ steps.endtest.outputs.test_cases }}
          PASSED: ${{ steps.endtest.outputs.passed }}
          FAILED: ${{ steps.endtest.outputs.failed }}
          ERRORS: ${{ steps.endtest.outputs.errors }}
          FAILED_TEST_CASES: ${{ steps.endtest.outputs.failed_test_cases }}
          HASHES: ${{ steps.endtest.outputs.hashes }}
          RESULT_URLS: ${{ steps.endtest.outputs.result_urls }}
          TEST_EXECUTIONS: ${{ steps.endtest.outputs.test_executions }}
        run: |
          echo "Executions: $EXECUTION_COUNT"
          echo "Test suites: $TEST_SUITE_NAMES"
          echo "Test cases: $TEST_CASES"
          echo "Passed assertions: $PASSED"
          echo "Failed assertions: $FAILED"
          echo "Errors: $ERRORS"
          echo "Failed test cases: $FAILED_TEST_CASES"
          echo "Hashes: $HASHES"
          echo "Result URLs: $RESULT_URLS"

          if [ -n "$TEST_EXECUTIONS" ]; then
            echo "$TEST_EXECUTIONS" | jq
          fi
```

The `if: always()` condition allows the results step to run even when `fail_build` causes the Endtest step to fail.

### Running one or more test suites

The `api_request` input accepts any valid Endtest API request for starting a test execution.

A request using `suite` normally starts one test suite:

```text
https://app.endtest.io/api.php?action=runWeb&appId=YOUR_APP_ID&appCode=YOUR_APP_CODE&suite=YOUR_SUITE_ID&platform=windows&os=windows11&browser=chrome&browserVersion=latest&resolution=1280x1024&geolocation=sanfrancisco&cases=all&notes=
```

A request using `label` can start multiple test suites:

```text
https://app.endtest.io/api.php?action=runWeb&appId=YOUR_APP_ID&appCode=YOUR_APP_CODE&label=Critical&platform=windows&os=windows11&browser=chrome&browserVersion=latest&resolution=1280x1024&geolocation=sanfrancisco&cases=all&notes=
```

When multiple test suites are triggered, Endtest returns multiple comma-separated execution hashes. The action sends all hashes to the Endtest results API and waits until a result is available for every execution.

### Inputs

* `app_id` `{string}`, required: The App ID for your Endtest account. It is available on the [Endtest Settings page](https://app.endtest.io/settings).
* `app_code` `{string}`, required: The App Code for your Endtest account. It is available on the [Endtest Settings page](https://app.endtest.io/settings).
* `api_request` `{string}`, required: The complete Endtest API request used to start one or more test executions.
* `number_of_loops` `{integer}`, required: The maximum number of times the action checks for results. Each check takes place after a 30-second interval.
* `results_format` `{string}`, optional: The results format returned by the Endtest API. Supported values are `json` and `json-light`. The default value is `json`.
* `fail_build` `{boolean}`, optional: Determines whether the GitHub Actions step fails when Endtest reports failed assertions, execution errors, or failed test cases. The default value is `false`.

We recommend setting `fail_build` to `true` when Endtest is used as a required CI check.

### Result formats

Use `json` when you need detailed execution logs and links to screenshots, browser logs, and video recordings.

Use `json-light` when you only need the execution summary and test case statuses. This results in a smaller API response.

When `json-light` is used, the `detailed_logs` and `screenshots_and_video` outputs are empty JSON arrays.

### Outputs

* `test_suite_name` `{string or JSON array}`: The test suite name for one execution, or a JSON array of test suite names when multiple executions were triggered.
* `configuration` `{string or JSON array}`: The execution configuration for one execution, or a JSON array of configurations when multiple executions were triggered.
* `test_cases` `{integer}`: The total number of test cases across all executions.
* `passed` `{integer}`: The total number of passed assertions reported across all executions.
* `failed` `{integer}`: The total number of failed assertions reported across all executions.
* `errors` `{integer}`: The total number of execution errors across all executions.
* `failed_test_cases` `{integer}`: The total number of test cases with a `Failed`, `Error`, or `Erred` status.
* `start_time` `{timestamp}`: The earliest start time across all executions.
* `end_time` `{timestamp}`: The latest end time across all executions.
* `detailed_logs` `{JSON string}`: A flattened JSON array containing detailed logs from all executions. This is empty when `results_format` is `json-light`.
* `screenshots_and_video` `{JSON string}`: A flattened JSON array containing screenshot, browser log, and video URLs from all executions. This is empty when `results_format` is `json-light`.
* `hash` `{string}`: The original execution hash response returned by Endtest. This may contain multiple comma-separated hashes.
* `results` `{string or JSON array}`: One Endtest Results page URL, or a JSON array of URLs when multiple executions were triggered.
* `execution_count` `{integer}`: The total number of completed Endtest executions.
* `hashes` `{JSON string}`: A JSON array containing every execution hash.
* `result_urls` `{JSON string}`: A JSON array containing an Endtest Results page URL for every execution.
* `test_executions` `{JSON string}`: The complete Endtest API response, normalized to a JSON array.

### Build failure behavior

When `fail_build` is set to `true`, the Endtest step fails if any of the following conditions are detected:

* One or more failed assertions
* One or more execution errors
* A test case with the status `Failed`
* A test case with the status `Error`
* A test case with the status `Erred`

The action writes its outputs before failing the step. You can therefore add a subsequent step with `if: always()` to print the results, upload artifacts, send notifications, or perform other cleanup actions.

> As an alternative, you can write your own custom script and use the Endtest API to start one or more test executions and fetch their results.
>
> More details are available in the [Endtest API](https://endtest.io/docs/advanced/how-to-use-the-endtest-api) chapter.

---

# Azure DevOps

Integrate Endtest with Azure DevOps Pipelines to trigger end-to-end tests on every build, publish results, and gate deployments on failures.

Part of the Endtest documentation (Integrations). Canonical URL: https://endtest.io/docs/integrations/azure-devops

---
## Overview

Integrate Endtest with Azure DevOps Pipelines to trigger automated end-to-end tests on every build, publish results in Azure DevOps, and prevent deployments when tests fail.

## Recommended approach: install the official Endtest extension

The easiest way to integrate Endtest with Azure DevOps is to install the official **Endtest for Azure DevOps** extension from the Visual Studio Marketplace:

[Install Endtest for Azure DevOps](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=endtest-technologies.endtest-azure-pipelines)

The extension adds the native `EndtestRun@1` pipeline task and an Endtest service connection type.

It can:

- Trigger one Endtest execution or multiple executions started through an Endtest label
- Store the Endtest App ID and App Code in a secure Azure DevOps service connection
- Wait for all Endtest executions to finish
- Publish an Endtest summary in the pipeline run
- Publish execution-level JUnit results in the Azure DevOps **Tests** section
- Expose execution hashes, result links, and test totals as output variables
- Fail the pipeline when Endtest reports failures or errors

The extension source code is available on [GitHub](https://github.com/endtest-technologies/endtest-azure-devops-extension).

## Install the extension

1. Open the [Endtest for Azure DevOps Marketplace page](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=endtest-technologies.endtest-azure-pipelines).
2. Select **Get it free**.
3. Choose the Azure DevOps organization where you want to install the extension.
4. Confirm the installation.
5. Open your Azure DevOps project.

You need permission to install extensions in the selected Azure DevOps organization.

## Create an Endtest service connection

After installing the extension:

1. Open your Azure DevOps project.
2. Go to **Project settings**.
3. Open **Service connections**.
4. Select **New service connection**.
5. Choose **Endtest**.
6. Set the Endtest URL to:

```text
https://app.endtest.io/
```

7. Enter your Endtest **App ID** and **App Code**.
8. Give the connection a recognizable name, such as:

```text
Endtest Production
```

9. Save the connection.

Using a service connection keeps the App Code out of your pipeline YAML. Credentials already included in the API request are still supported for backward compatibility, but the service connection is recommended.

## Add Endtest to an Azure Pipeline

Add the `EndtestRun@1` task to your pipeline:

```yaml
steps:
  - task: EndtestRun@1
    name: runEndtest
    displayName: Run Endtest tests
    inputs:
      endtestService: 'Endtest Production'
      apiRequest: 'https://app.endtest.io/api.php?action=runWeb&suite=YOUR_SUITE_ID&platform=windows&os=windows11&browser=chrome&browserVersion=latest&resolution=1280x1024&geolocation=sanfrancisco&cases=all&notes='
      timeoutMinutes: '30'
      pollIntervalSeconds: '30'
      resultsFormat: 'json-light'
      failPipeline: true
      publishSummary: true
      publishTestResults: true
      testRunTitle: 'Endtest automated tests'
```

Replace `YOUR_SUITE_ID` and the other configuration parameters with the values from the API request generated in Endtest.

The App ID and App Code can normally be omitted from `apiRequest`. The task adds them from the selected service connection when they are not already present.

## Task inputs

| Input | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `endtestService` | No | None | Recommended Endtest service connection containing the App ID and App Code. |
| `apiRequest` | Yes | None | Complete Endtest API request used to start the execution. |
| `timeoutMinutes` | Yes | `30` | Maximum time to wait for the Endtest execution. Allowed range: 1 to 1440 minutes. |
| `pollIntervalSeconds` | Yes | `30` | Time between result checks. Allowed range: 5 to 300 seconds. |
| `resultsFormat` | Yes | `json-light` | Use `json-light` for normal pipeline runs or `json` when detailed logs and media data are needed. |
| `failPipeline` | No | `true` | Fails the Azure Pipeline when Endtest reports failures or errors. |
| `publishSummary` | No | `true` | Adds an Endtest summary to the pipeline run. |
| `publishTestResults` | No | `true` | Publishes one Azure DevOps test result for each Endtest execution. |
| `testRunTitle` | No | `Endtest automated tests` | Title used for the Azure DevOps test run. |

## Pipeline results

When the Endtest execution finishes, the task can publish:

- The test suite name and configuration
- The number of test cases
- Passed, failed, and error totals
- Start and end times
- Direct links to the Endtest results
- JUnit results in the Azure DevOps **Tests** section

When `failPipeline` is enabled, the task fails the pipeline if Endtest reports a failure or error. This allows the task to act as a deployment gate.

## Output variables

Assign a name to the task, such as `runEndtest`, to use its output variables in later steps:

```yaml
- script: |
    echo "Executions: $(runEndtest.executionCount)"
    echo "Hashes: $(runEndtest.hashes)"
    echo "Results: $(runEndtest.resultUrls)"
    echo "Status: $(runEndtest.status)"
  displayName: Show Endtest outputs
  condition: always()
```

The following output variables are available:

- `$(runEndtest.executionCount)`
- `$(runEndtest.hashes)`
- `$(runEndtest.resultUrls)`
- `$(runEndtest.testCases)`
- `$(runEndtest.passed)`
- `$(runEndtest.failed)`
- `$(runEndtest.errors)`
- `$(runEndtest.status)`

## Running multiple Endtest executions

An Endtest API request can start more than one execution, for example when a label is used to run several configurations.

The Azure DevOps task detects all returned execution hashes, waits for every execution to finish, includes all result links in the pipeline summary, and publishes one Azure DevOps test result for each execution.

## Manual integration with a Shell Script task

The Marketplace extension is recommended for most teams because it handles credentials, polling, summaries, Azure DevOps test-result publishing, output variables, and pipeline failure behavior.

You can still use the original do-it-yourself approach when you need a fully custom implementation or cannot install Marketplace extensions in your Azure DevOps organization.

You can use the [Endtest API](https://endtest.io/docs/advanced/how-to-use-the-endtest-api/) and a [Shell Script task](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/tasks/utility/shell-script?view=azure-devops) to integrate Endtest with Azure DevOps.

The following video demonstrates the manual integration method:

[Video](https://endtest-videos.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/documentation/endtest_azure_devops_docs.mp4)

### YAML snippet

```yaml
trigger:
- main

pool:
  vmImage: ubuntu-latest

steps:
- task: Bash@3
  inputs:
    filePath: 'test.sh'
    arguments: 'app-id app-code "api-request-to-start-test-execution" number-of-loops'
```

Create `test.sh` at the root of your repo.

We recommend creating this file from a Linux environment, such as a real Linux machine or Windows Subsystem for Linux, so that line endings are correct.

Also, do not forget to run `chmod +x test.sh` before you commit it.

### `test.sh`

```bash
#!/bin/bash
hash=$(curl -X GET --header "Accept: */*" "${3}")
for run in {1.."${4}"}
do
  sleep 30
  result=$(curl -X GET --header "Accept: */*" "https://app.endtest.io/api.php?action=getResults&appId=${1}&appCode=${2}&hash=${hash}&format=json")
  if [ "$result" == "Test is still running." ]
  then
    status=$result
    # Don't print anything
  elif [ "$result" == "Processing video recording." ]
  then
    status=$result
    # Don't print anything
  elif [ "$result" == "Stopping." ]
  then
    status=$result
  elif [ "$result" == "Erred." ]
  then
    status=$result
    echo $status
  elif [ "$result" == "" ]
  then
    status=$result
    # Don't print anything
  else
     echo "$result" | jq
     exit 0
  fi
done
exit
```

This sample script requires the following arguments:

1. The `App ID` for your account.
2. The `App Code` for your account.
3. The API Request for starting the test execution.
4. The number of times the API request for fetching the results will be sent, once every 30 seconds.

For example, if you know that your test execution usually takes 3 minutes, you should use the value 7.

```text
7 x 30 seconds = 210 seconds > 3 minutes
```

Make the Shell script executable by running:

```bash
sudo chmod +x test.sh
```

You also need to install the `jq` package:

```bash
sudo apt-get install jq
```

The command for running the `test.sh` script locally has the following format:

```bash
./test.sh app-id app-code api-request-to-start-test-execution number-of-loops
```

For example, consider the following values:

```text
App ID = 44233559

App Code = 22381137

Endtest API Request to start test execution = "https://app.endtest.io/api.php?action=runWeb&appId=44233559&appCode=22381137&suite=380667&platform=windows&os=windows10&browser=chrome&browserVersion=latest&resolution=1280x1024&geolocation=sanfrancisco&cases=all&notes="

Number of loops = 10
```

The command for running the `test.sh` script locally would look like this:

```bash
./test.sh 44233559 22381137 "https://app.endtest.io/api.php?action=runWeb&appId=44233559&appCode=22381137&suite=380667&platform=windows&os=windows10&browser=chrome&browserVersion=latest&resolution=1280x1024&geolocation=sanfrancisco&cases=all&notes=" 10
```

The YAML file in Azure DevOps would look like this:

```yaml
trigger:
- main

pool:
  vmImage: ubuntu-latest

steps:
- task: Bash@3
  inputs:
    filePath: 'test.sh'
    arguments: '44233559 22381137 "https://app.endtest.io/api.php?action=runWeb&appId=44233559&appCode=22381137&suite=380667&platform=windows&os=windows10&browser=chrome&browserVersion=latest&resolution=1280x1024&geolocation=sanfrancisco&cases=all&notes=" 10'
```

> Since you will be integrating Endtest into your current Azure DevOps Pipeline, your actual YAML file will also contain existing instructions that are not related to Endtest.
>
> It will also contain instructions to read the JSON output from the Endtest API response and execute the required pipeline logic, such as marking a build as passed or failed.

The JSON with the results contains the following keys:

- `test_suite_name`: The name of the test suite.
- `configuration`: The configuration of the machine or mobile device on which the test was executed.
- `test_cases`: The number of test cases.
- `passed`: The number of assertions that have passed.
- `failed`: The number of assertions that have failed.
- `errors`: The number of errors that have been encountered.
- `start_time`: The timestamp for the start of the test execution.
- `end_time`: The timestamp for the end of the test execution.
- `detailed_logs`: The detailed logs for the test execution.
- `screenshots_and_video`: The URLs for the screenshots and the video recording of the test execution.
- `test_case_management`: The name, status, and external IDs for each test case.

You can also use the value of the `hash` variable to generate the link to the Results page for that test execution:

```bash
results=https://app.endtest.io/results?hash="$hash"
```

More details about the API are available in the [Endtest API](https://endtest.io/docs/advanced/how-to-use-the-endtest-api/) chapter.

## Troubleshooting

### The `EndtestRun@1` task is not found

Confirm that the extension is installed in the same Azure DevOps organization where the pipeline is running.

### Authentication fails

Check the App ID and App Code in the selected Endtest service connection. Also confirm that the pipeline is authorized to use that service connection.

### The execution exceeds the pipeline timeout

Increase `timeoutMinutes` or verify that the Endtest execution is not waiting indefinitely for an unavailable browser, device, or environment.

### Detailed Endtest logs are missing

Change `resultsFormat` from `json-light` to `json`. The lighter format is recommended for normal runs because it returns less data.

### The pipeline passes even though a test should block deployment

Confirm that `failPipeline` is set to `true` and that Endtest returned a failure or error in the final result.

# CircleCI

Run Endtest end-to-end tests in CircleCI with the official Endtest orb

Part of the Endtest documentation (Integrations). Canonical URL: https://endtest.io/docs/integrations/circleci

---
## Overview

The official Endtest CircleCI orb allows you to run Endtest web and mobile tests directly from a CircleCI workflow.

The orb can:

- Start one or more Endtest test executions.
- Wait for all executions to finish.
- Display the result of each execution in CircleCI.
- Display aggregate results when multiple test suites are triggered.
- Fail the CircleCI job when any execution reports failed assertions or errors.
- Block a deployment when an important end-to-end test fails.

You can view the orb in the [CircleCI Orb Registry](https://circleci.com/developer/orbs/orb/endtest/endtest).

The source code is available in the [Endtest CircleCI Orb repository](https://github.com/endtest-technologies/endtest-circleci-orb).

## Requirements

Before using the orb, you need:

1. An Endtest account.
2. Your Endtest `App ID`.
3. Your Endtest `App Code`.
4. An Endtest API Request for starting the desired test execution.
5. A CircleCI project connected to your source-code repository.

Your `App ID` and `App Code` can be found on the [Endtest Settings page](https://app.endtest.io/settings).

You can generate an API Request by following the instructions from the [Endtest API](https://endtest.io/docs/advanced/how-to-use-the-endtest-api) chapter.

The API Request added to the CircleCI configuration must not contain the `appId` or `appCode` parameters. The orb adds those values securely at runtime.

## Add the environment variables

Open your project in CircleCI and navigate to:

```text
Project Settings → Environment Variables
```

Add these environment variables:

```text
ENDTEST_APP_ID
ENDTEST_APP_CODE
```

Their values should be:

- `ENDTEST_APP_ID`: The App ID for your Endtest account.
- `ENDTEST_APP_CODE`: The App Code for your Endtest account.

CircleCI hides the values of environment variables after they are saved.

The Endtest API Request itself is added visibly to `.circleci/config.yml`, without credentials. This allows team members to see which test suite, label, browser, operating system, resolution, and other settings are being used.

## Add the Endtest orb

Create or update the `.circleci/config.yml` file in your repository:

```yaml
version: 2.1

orbs:
  endtest: endtest/endtest@0.0.7

workflows:
  endtest-tests:
    jobs:
      - endtest/run:
          api_request: 'https://app.endtest.io/api.php?action=runWeb&suite=YOUR_SUITE_ID&platform=windows&os=windows11&browser=chrome&browserVersion=latest&resolution=1280x1024&geolocation=sanfrancisco&cases=all&notes='
          number_of_loops: 10
```

Replace `YOUR_SUITE_ID` with the ID of the Endtest test suite you want to execute.

Do not add `appId` or `appCode` to the API Request. The orb reads them from the CircleCI environment variables and adds them securely.

Always check the [Endtest page in the CircleCI Orb Registry](https://circleci.com/developer/orbs/orb/endtest/endtest) for the latest published version.

## Trigger multiple test suites

An Endtest API Request can trigger multiple test suites by using a label instead of a suite ID.

For example:

```yaml
version: 2.1

orbs:
  endtest: endtest/endtest@0.0.7

workflows:
  critical-tests:
    jobs:
      - endtest/run:
          api_request: 'https://app.endtest.io/api.php?action=runWeb&label=Critical&platform=windows&os=windows11&browser=chrome&browserVersion=latest&resolution=1280x1024&geolocation=sanfrancisco&cases=all&notes='
          number_of_loops: 10
```

This request starts every test suite associated with the `Critical` label.

The Endtest API may return multiple execution hashes:

```text
EXECUTION_HASH_1,EXECUTION_HASH_2
```

The orb automatically:

1. Detects every execution hash.
2. Waits for all test executions to finish.
3. Displays the result of each test suite separately.
4. Calculates aggregate totals.
5. Fails the CircleCI job if any execution reports failures or errors.

No additional CircleCI configuration is required for multiple test executions.

## Using the default environment-variable names

The default credential environment-variable names are:

```text
ENDTEST_APP_ID
ENDTEST_APP_CODE
```

When you use these names, you do not need to pass the `app_id` or `app_code` parameters:

```yaml
version: 2.1

orbs:
  endtest: endtest/endtest@0.0.7

workflows:
  endtest-tests:
    jobs:
      - endtest/run:
          api_request: 'https://app.endtest.io/api.php?action=runWeb&label=Critical&platform=windows&os=windows11&browser=chrome&browserVersion=latest&resolution=1280x1024&geolocation=sanfrancisco&cases=all&notes='
          number_of_loops: 10
```

## Using custom credential variable names

You can use different names for the credential environment variables:

```yaml
version: 2.1

orbs:
  endtest: endtest/endtest@0.0.7

workflows:
  endtest-tests:
    jobs:
      - endtest/run:
          app_id: MY_ENDTEST_APP_ID
          app_code: MY_ENDTEST_APP_CODE
          api_request: 'https://app.endtest.io/api.php?action=runWeb&label=Critical&platform=windows&os=windows11&browser=chrome&browserVersion=latest&resolution=1280x1024&geolocation=sanfrancisco&cases=all&notes='
          number_of_loops: 10
```

In that case, add these variables to the CircleCI project:

```text
MY_ENDTEST_APP_ID
MY_ENDTEST_APP_CODE
```

The values passed to `app_id` and `app_code` are the names of CircleCI environment variables, not the actual credentials.

## Legacy environment-variable configuration

Older versions of the Endtest orb expected the entire API Request to be stored in an environment variable named:

```text
ENDTEST_API_REQUEST
```

Version `0.0.7` continues to support this configuration for compatibility.

When the visible `api_request` parameter is not provided, the orb reads the complete request from `ENDTEST_API_REQUEST`.

The recommended configuration is to keep only the App ID and App Code in environment variables and place the API Request without credentials in `.circleci/config.yml`.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `app_id` | Environment-variable name | `ENDTEST_APP_ID` | The variable containing your Endtest App ID. |
| `app_code` | Environment-variable name | `ENDTEST_APP_CODE` | The variable containing your Endtest App Code. |
| `api_request` | String | Empty | A visible Endtest API Request without `appId` or `appCode`. |
| `api_request_env_var` | Environment-variable name | `ENDTEST_API_REQUEST` | Legacy fallback variable containing the complete API Request. |
| `number_of_loops` | Integer | `10` | Maximum number of result checks. Each check occurs after a 30-second wait. |

The `api_request` parameter takes priority over `api_request_env_var`.

For security, the visible API Request must use:

```text
https://app.endtest.io/api.php
```

The orb rejects visible requests that contain `appId` or `appCode`.

## Choosing the number of loops

The orb checks the Endtest execution once every 30 seconds.

For example, when an execution normally takes approximately three minutes, you can use:

```yaml
number_of_loops: 7
```

This allows up to 210 seconds:

```text
7 × 30 seconds = 210 seconds
```

Choose a value slightly higher than the normal duration of the test execution.

When a request triggers multiple test suites, set the value according to the longest-running execution.

For tests that normally finish within five minutes, you can use:

```yaml
number_of_loops: 10
```

## Pipeline behavior

The CircleCI job passes when every completed Endtest execution reports:

```text
Failed: 0
Errors: 0
```

The job fails when:

- Any execution reports one or more failed assertions.
- Any execution reports one or more errors.
- An execution enters an error state.
- The API returns an invalid response.
- The number of returned results does not match the number of started executions.
- The executions do not finish within the configured polling period.

## Use Endtest as a deployment gate

The `endtest/run` job can be used as a deployment gate:

```yaml
version: 2.1

orbs:
  endtest: endtest/endtest@0.0.7

jobs:
  deploy:
    docker:
      - image: cimg/base:stable
    steps:
      - run:
          name: Deploy application
          command: ./deploy.sh

workflows:
  test-and-deploy:
    jobs:
      - endtest/run:
          name: endtest-tests
          api_request: 'https://app.endtest.io/api.php?action=runWeb&label=Critical&platform=windows&os=windows11&browser=chrome&browserVersion=latest&resolution=1280x1024&geolocation=sanfrancisco&cases=all&notes='
          number_of_loops: 10

      - deploy:
          requires:
            - endtest-tests
```

The `deploy` job only starts when all Endtest executions pass.

## Results displayed in CircleCI

For every Endtest execution, the orb displays:

- Test suite name.
- Test configuration.
- Number of test cases.
- Number of passed assertions.
- Number of failed assertions.
- Number of errors.
- Start time.
- End time.
- Execution hash.
- Link to the Endtest Results page.

When multiple test suites are triggered, the orb also displays an aggregate summary:

```text
Endtest summary
Executions: 2
Test Cases: 4
Passed: 12
Failed: 0
Errors: 0
```

The Results page for an execution has the following format:

```text
https://app.endtest.io/results?hash=EXECUTION_HASH
```

## Manual API integration

The official orb is the recommended way to integrate Endtest with CircleCI.

For custom workflows that cannot use an orb, you can call the Endtest API directly from a shell script. The script must:

1. Send the API Request that starts one or more test executions.
2. Save the execution hash or comma-separated execution hashes returned by Endtest.
3. Call the `getResults` API endpoint using the App ID, App Code, and execution hashes.
4. Continue checking until every execution finishes.
5. Return a non-zero exit code when any execution fails.

More information about direct API usage is available in the [Endtest API](../advanced/how-to-use-the-endtest-api) chapter.

## Additional resources

- [Endtest CircleCI Orb](https://circleci.com/developer/orbs/orb/endtest/endtest)
- [Endtest CircleCI Orb source code](https://github.com/endtest-technologies/endtest-circleci-orb)
- [Endtest API documentation](../advanced/how-to-use-the-endtest-api)
- [Endtest Settings](https://app.endtest.io/settings)

# TravisCI

Integrate Endtest with Travis CI to run automated end-to-end tests on every push and gate merges on test results, without managing browser infrastructure.

Part of the Endtest documentation (Integrations). Canonical URL: https://endtest.io/docs/integrations/travisci

---
## Instructions

You can use the [Endtest API](https://endtest.io/docs/advanced/how-to-use-the-endtest-api/) in your TravisCI workflow.

This can be done by creating a `test.sh` file and executing it from your TravisCI workflow.

**.travis/yml**
```yaml
test:
  provider: script
  script: bash scripts/test.sh
  on:
    branch: develop
```
**test.sh**
```sh
#!/bin/bash
hash=$(curl -X GET --header "Accept: */*" "${3}")
for run in {1.."${4}"}
do
  sleep 30
  result=$(curl -X GET --header "Accept: */*" "https://app.endtest.io/api.php?action=getResults&appId=${1}&appCode=${2}&hash=${hash}&format=json")
  if [ "$result" == "Test is still running." ]
  then
    status=$result
    # Don't print anything
  elif [ "$result" == "Processing video recording." ]
  then
    status=$result
    # Don't print anything
  elif [ "$result" == "Stopping." ]
  then
    status=$result
  elif [ "$result" == "Erred." ]
  then
    status=$result
    echo $status
  elif [ "$result" == "" ]
  then
    status=$result
    # Don't print anything
  else
     echo "$result" | jq
     exit 0
  fi
done
exit
```

This sample script would require the following arguments:
1. The `App ID` for your account.
2. The `App Code` for your account.
3. The API Request for starting the test execution.
4. The number of times the API request for fetching the results will be sent once every 30 seconds.

For example, if you know that your test execution usually takes 3 minutes, you should use the value 7.

`7 x 30 seconds = 210 seconds > 3 minutes`

Don't forget to make your Shell script executable by running the following command:

```console
sudo chmod +x test.sh
```

And you would also need to install the `jq` package:

```sh
sudo apt-get install jq
```

The command for running the sample Shell script would have the following format:

```sh
./test.sh app-id app-code api-request-to-start-test-execution number-of-loops
```

Let's pretend we have the following values:

```
App ID = 44233559

App Code = 22381137

Endtest API Request to start test execution = "https://app.endtest.io/api.php?action=runWeb&appId=44233559&appCode=22381137&suite=380667&platform=windows&os=windows10&browser=chrome&browserVersion=latest&resolution=1280x1024&geolocation=sanfrancisco&cases=all&notes="

Number of loops = 10
```

The command for running the sample Shell script would look like this:

```sh
./test.sh 44233559 22381137 "https://app.endtest.io/api.php?action=runWeb&appId=44233559&appCode=22381137&suite=380667&platform=windows&os=windows10&browser=chrome&browserVersion=latest&resolution=1280x1024&geolocation=sanfrancisco&cases=all&notes=" 10
```

The JSON with the results contains the following keys:

* `test_suite_name` `{string}` - The name of the test suite.
* `configuration` `{string}` - The configuration of the machine or mobile device on which the test was executed.
* `test_cases` `{int32}` - The number of test cases.
* `passed` `{int32}` - The number of assertions that have passed.
* `failed` `{int32}` - The number of assertions that have failed.
* `errors` `{int32}` - The number of errors that have been encountered.
* `start_time` `{timestamp}` - The timestamp for the start of the test execution.
* `end_time` `{timestamp}` - The timestamp for the end of the test execution.
* `detailed_logs` `{string}` - The detailed logs for the test execution.
* `screenshots_and_video` `{string}` - The URLs for the screenshots and the video recording of the test execution.
* `test_case_management` `{string}` - The name, status and external IDs for each test case. 

You can also use the value of the `hash` variable to generate the link to the Results page for that test execution:

```sh
results=https://app.endtest.io/results?hash="$hash"
```

>You can find more details about our API in the [Endtest API](https://endtest.io/docs/advanced/how-to-use-the-endtest-api/) chapter.

# Netlify

Run one or multiple Endtest test suites after Netlify deployments with the official Endtest extension

Part of the Endtest documentation (Integrations). Canonical URL: https://endtest.io/docs/integrations/netlify

---
## Overview

The official Endtest Netlify extension allows you to run Endtest web tests automatically after a successful Netlify deployment.

The extension can:

- Start one Endtest test suite after a deployment goes live.
- Start multiple Endtest test suites in the same API call by using a label.
- Wait for every triggered execution to finish.
- Display the Endtest results in the Netlify deploy log.
- Report failed assertions and execution errors as an extension failure.
- Use a separate Endtest configuration for each Netlify project.
- Pass the current Netlify deployment URL to Endtest.

You can install the extension from the [Endtest page in the Netlify Extensions Directory](https://app.netlify.com/extensions/0e7j1jxj-endtest-netlify-extension).

The source code is available in the [Endtest Netlify Extension repository](https://github.com/endtest-technologies/endtest-netlify-extension).

## Requirements

Before using the extension, you need:

1. An Endtest account.
2. Your Endtest `App ID`.
3. Your Endtest `App Code`.
4. An Endtest API Request for starting the desired test execution or executions.
5. A Netlify account.
6. A Netlify project.

Your `App ID` and `App Code` can be found on the [Endtest Settings page](https://app.endtest.io/settings).

You can generate the API Request by following the instructions from the [Endtest API](https://endtest.io/docs/advanced/how-to-use-the-endtest-api) chapter.

## Install the Endtest extension

Open the [Endtest extension page on Netlify](https://app.netlify.com/extensions/0e7j1jxj-endtest-netlify-extension) and select **Install**.

Choose the Netlify team that contains the project where you want to use Endtest.

During installation, the extension requests permission to read, write, and delete project environment variables.

These permissions are used to:

- Save the Endtest configuration for each Netlify project.
- Enable or disable Endtest for a project.
- Read the saved configuration during a deployment.

The extension does not require access to your source-code repository.

## Configure Endtest for a Netlify project

After installing the extension:

1. Open the desired project in Netlify.
2. Select **Endtest** from the project navigation.
3. Enter your Endtest `App ID`.
4. Enter your Endtest `App Code`.
5. Paste the Endtest API Request.
6. Choose the maximum number of result checks.
7. Select **Save and enable Endtest**.

The Endtest configuration is stored separately for each Netlify project.

The extension creates and manages the following project-level environment variables:

```text
ENDTEST_ENABLED
ENDTEST_APP_ID
ENDTEST_APP_CODE
ENDTEST_API_REQUEST
ENDTEST_NUMBER_OF_LOOPS
```

These values are stored in Netlify and are not committed to your website repository.

## Endtest API Request

The API Request determines which Endtest test suite or test suites will run.

A typical API Request can include:

- Test suite or label.
- Browser.
- Browser version.
- Operating system.
- Screen resolution.
- Geolocation.
- Test cases.
- Execution notes.

You do not need to include `appId` or `appCode` in the saved API Request.

The extension automatically adds the `App ID` and `App Code` from the project configuration before starting the execution.

More information about supported API parameters is available in the [Endtest API](https://endtest.io/docs/advanced/how-to-use-the-endtest-api) chapter.

## Run a single test suite

Use the `suite` parameter to run one Endtest test suite.

Example:

```text
https://app.endtest.io/api.php?action=runWeb&suite=2945352&platform=windows&os=windows11&browser=chrome&browserVersion=latest&resolution=1280x1024&geolocation=sanfrancisco&cases=all&notes=
```

The Endtest API returns one execution hash:

```text
71frWqyL1YdAVfvlP63DgZ4TGYewnJoOij
```

The extension uses that hash to check the execution result until the test finishes or the configured polling period expires.

## Run multiple test suites with a label

Use the `label` parameter to run every Endtest test suite associated with the specified label.

Example:

```text
https://app.endtest.io/api.php?action=runWeb&label=Critical&platform=windows&os=windows11&browser=chrome&browserVersion=latest&resolution=1280x1024&geolocation=sanfrancisco&cases=all&notes=
```

In this example, Endtest starts every test suite associated with the `Critical` label.

The API returns the execution hashes as a comma-separated value:

```text
Udq2dphebLjy29dQr63xe7ZmPGkNZvz3T5,QNHWpc98OE6699qXg63SF2K8KIabRk9bLy
```

The extension:

1. Reads all returned execution hashes.
2. Sends all hashes to the Endtest `getResults` API endpoint.
3. Waits until a result is available for every execution.
4. Displays the individual result for every test suite.
5. Calculates combined failure and error totals.
6. Marks the extension as failed when any execution reports failed assertions, execution errors, or a failure status.

The extension uses a results request with the following structure:

```text
https://app.endtest.io/api.php?action=getResults&appId=APP_ID&appCode=APP_CODE&hash=HASH_1,HASH_2&format=json-light
```

The `json-light` response contains one result object for each execution:

```json
[
  {
    "test_suite_name": "Online Store with AI",
    "configuration": "Windows 11 Chrome Latest (v149) 1280 x 1024 San Francisco, US",
    "test_cases": 1,
    "passed": 0,
    "failed": 0,
    "errors": 0
  },
  {
    "test_suite_name": "Demo Shop",
    "configuration": "Windows 11 Chrome Latest (v149) 1280 x 1024 San Francisco, US",
    "test_cases": 1,
    "passed": 0,
    "failed": 0,
    "errors": 0
  }
]
```

The same extension configuration supports both single-suite and label-based executions. You only need to change the saved API Request.

## Use the current Netlify deployment URL

You can include the following placeholder anywhere inside the Endtest API Request:

```text
{{NETLIFY_DEPLOY_URL}}
```

Before starting the Endtest execution, the extension replaces the placeholder with the URL of the current Netlify deployment.

Example:

```text
https://app.endtest.io/api.php?action=runWeb&suite=123456&startUrl={{NETLIFY_DEPLOY_URL}}
```

The placeholder can also be used in a label-based request:

```text
https://app.endtest.io/api.php?action=runWeb&label=Critical&startUrl={{NETLIFY_DEPLOY_URL}}
```

This can be used to run tests against:

- Production deployments.
- Branch deployments.
- Deploy Previews.

The exact API parameter used for the start URL depends on how your Endtest test is configured.

## Choosing the number of result checks

The extension checks the Endtest execution results once every 30 seconds.

For example, when an execution normally takes approximately three minutes, you can use:

```text
Maximum result checks: 7
```

This allows up to 210 seconds:

```text
7 × 30 seconds = 210 seconds
```

Choose a value that is slightly higher than the normal duration of the slowest triggered test suite.

For a group of test suites that usually finishes within five minutes, you can use:

```text
Maximum result checks: 10
```

When multiple test suites are triggered, the extension continues polling until every execution has returned a final result.

If one or more executions do not finish within the configured polling period, the extension reports a timeout.

## Deployment behavior

The Endtest extension runs after the Netlify deployment has completed successfully.

For a single execution, the extension reports success when Endtest returns:

```text
Failed: 0
Errors: 0
```

For multiple executions, every result must contain:

```text
Failed: 0
Errors: 0
```

The extension reports a failure when:

- Any execution reports one or more failed assertions.
- Any execution reports one or more execution errors.
- Any execution enters an error or failure state.
- The API returns an invalid response.
- The API does not return a result for every triggered execution.
- One or more executions do not finish within the configured polling period.

A failed Endtest execution is displayed as an extension failure in the Netlify deploy log.

When multiple test suites are triggered, one failed suite causes the complete Endtest extension run to be marked as failed.

## Important limitation

Endtest runs after the Netlify deployment has completed. If Endtest reports failed assertions or execution errors, the extension is marked as failed in the deploy log, but the completed deployment remains live and is not removed, canceled, or rolled back.

This behavior allows Endtest to test the actual deployed URL.

The Netlify extension should therefore be used for post-deployment validation rather than as a deployment gate.

## Results displayed in Netlify

For a single execution, the extension can display information such as:

- Execution hash.
- Netlify deployment URL.
- Test suite name.
- Test configuration.
- Number of test cases.
- Number of passed assertions.
- Number of failed assertions.
- Number of execution errors.

Example:

```text
Execution hash: abc123
Netlify deployment: https://example.netlify.app
Test suite: Demo Shop
Configuration: Windows 11 Chrome Latest 1280 x 1024
Test cases: 5
Passed: 12
Failed: 0
Errors: 0
```

For multiple executions, the extension displays a combined summary followed by the result of each test suite.

Example:

```text
Executions: 2
Execution hashes: HASH_1, HASH_2
Netlify deployment: https://example.netlify.app
Total failed: 0
Total errors: 0

Execution 1 of 2
Execution hash: HASH_1
Test suite: Online Store with AI
Configuration: Windows 11 Chrome Latest 1280 x 1024
Test cases: 1
Passed: 0
Failed: 0
Errors: 0

Execution 2 of 2
Execution hash: HASH_2
Test suite: Demo Shop
Configuration: Windows 11 Chrome Latest 1280 x 1024
Test cases: 1
Passed: 0
Failed: 0
Errors: 0
```

The Endtest API response may contain the following fields:

- `test_suite_name` `{string}`: The name of the test suite.
- `configuration` `{string}`: The machine or mobile-device configuration used for the execution.
- `test_cases` `{int32}`: The number of test cases.
- `passed` `{int32}`: The number of assertions that passed.
- `failed` `{int32}`: The number of assertions that failed.
- `errors` `{int32}`: The number of execution errors.
- `start_time` `{timestamp}`: The execution start time.
- `end_time` `{timestamp}`: The execution end time.
- `detailed_logs` `{string}`: The detailed execution logs when the `json` format is used.
- `screenshots_and_video` `{string}`: Links to screenshots and video recordings when the `json` format is used.
- `test_case_management` `{string}`: The names, statuses, and external IDs of associated test cases.

The Results page for an execution has the following format:

```text
https://app.endtest.io/results?hash=EXECUTION_HASH
```

Each execution in a label-based run has its own Endtest Results page and execution hash.

## Tests without assertions

An Endtest execution can contain test steps without assertions.

In that case, the result can contain:

```text
Passed: 0
Failed: 0
Errors: 0
```

This is still considered a successful execution because Endtest reported no failed assertions and no execution errors.

The same behavior applies to multiple executions. Every execution can report zero passed assertions and still be successful when `failed` and `errors` are both zero.

## Disable Endtest for a project

To disable the integration:

1. Open the Netlify project.
2. Select **Endtest**.
3. Select **Disable Endtest**.

Disabling Endtest stops new executions for that project.

The saved `App ID`, `App Code`, and API Request are preserved, so the integration can be enabled again without re-entering the configuration.

## Security

The Endtest configuration is stored as project-level Netlify environment variables.

The credentials are not committed to the website repository.

The extension hides the `App Code` when it displays the API Request in the deploy log.

Because `ENDTEST_APP_CODE` is stored as a standard Netlify environment variable, users with sufficient access to the Netlify project may be able to view or edit it from the project settings.

## Troubleshooting

### Endtest does not run after a deployment

Check that:

- The Endtest extension is installed for the correct Netlify team.
- Endtest is enabled for the project.
- The `App ID` is correct.
- The `App Code` is correct.
- The API Request is a complete HTTPS URL.
- The Netlify deployment completed successfully.

The extension only starts Endtest after a successful deployment.

### Only one test suite runs

Check the saved API Request.

A request containing:

```text
suite=123456
```

runs one specific test suite.

To run multiple test suites, use a label:

```text
label=Critical
```

Every Endtest test suite associated with that label will be triggered.

### The configuration cannot be saved

Confirm that the extension has permission to read, write, and delete project environment variables.

If the permissions were changed after the extension was installed, uninstall and reinstall the extension so the installation receives the updated permissions.

### The API Request is rejected

Make sure that:

- The request starts with `https://`.
- The request uses a valid Endtest API action.
- The suite ID or label is valid.
- The browser, operating system, and other configuration parameters are supported.
- The API Request does not need to contain `appId` or `appCode`, because the extension adds them automatically.

### One or more execution results are missing

When a label triggers multiple test suites, Endtest returns multiple execution hashes.

The extension waits until the results response contains one final result for every returned hash.

If some executions take longer than others, increase the **Maximum result checks** value.

### The execution times out

Increase the **Maximum result checks** value.

Each result check occurs after a 30-second wait.

For example:

```text
10 checks × 30 seconds = 300 seconds
```

For label-based runs, choose a value that allows enough time for the slowest test suite to finish.

### The deployment remains live after a failed test

This is expected.

The Endtest extension runs after deployment so it can test the actual deployed URL.

A failed Endtest execution marks the extension as failed in the deploy log, but it cannot undo a deployment that has already completed.

## Manual API integration

The official Endtest extension is the recommended way to integrate Endtest with Netlify.

For custom workflows, you can call the Endtest API directly from a script or Netlify Function.

The custom integration must:

1. Send the API Request that starts the test execution or executions.
2. Save the execution hash or comma-separated execution hashes returned by Endtest.
3. Call the `getResults` API endpoint using the `App ID`, `App Code`, and returned hashes.
4. Continue checking until every execution finishes.
5. Report a failure when any execution returns failed assertions or execution errors.

For multiple executions, the results request has the following structure:

```text
https://app.endtest.io/api.php?action=getResults&appId=APP_ID&appCode=APP_CODE&hash=HASH_1,HASH_2&format=json-light
```

More information about direct API usage is available in the [Endtest API](https://endtest.io/docs/advanced/how-to-use-the-endtest-api) chapter.

## Additional resources

- [Install the Endtest Netlify extension](https://app.netlify.com/extensions/0e7j1jxj-endtest-netlify-extension)
- [Endtest Netlify Extension source code](https://github.com/endtest-technologies/endtest-netlify-extension)
- [Endtest API documentation](https://endtest.io/docs/advanced/how-to-use-the-endtest-api)
- [Endtest Settings](https://app.endtest.io/settings)
- [Endtest website](https://endtest.io/)
